docs.title: Sojourn documentation
docs.text: Sojourn is in development. These pages cover what is in the package today and grow with every sprint.

docs.title: Start here: three steps to your first report, about 25 minutes
docs.text:
1. Install Sojourn About 10 minutesInstall the package in a sandbox or production org and open the Sojourn app.
  2. Assign permission sets About 5 minutesGive admins, managers, and everyone else the access Sojourn needs.
  3. Track Cases and open your first report About 10 minutesTurn on tracking for Case status and owner, then open the Time in Status by Case report.

docs.title: New here?
docs.text:
Sojourn records how long every record spends in each status and with each owner, in business hours, as plain rows you can report on. Each Tracked field gets its own lane.

Sample data. The Coral part of the Status lane is time past the Goal.

docs.title: Sprint 15: Get started (1 November 2026)
docs.text:
• Get started. The first time an admin opens Sojourn Settings after install, it opens on a guide of twelve steps in four phases. Each step shows what Sojourn found in your org just now, why the step matters, and a button to the screen where you do it. Check again reads every step again. Steps 11 and 12 are changes in Setup and Lightning App Builder that Sojourn cannot read, so you mark them done by hand. Step 4 done offers Add another object, which opens Tracked objects with the Add object dialog open, through a new link, c__screen=objects&c__section=add (see Links into Sojourn). See Use the Get started guide.
  • The switch and the banner. Open this guide first when Sojourn Settings opens is on after install and turns itself off once every required step is done. While steps remain, the Overview opens with a banner that names the steps still to go, and the Get started line in the menu shows a count such as 3 of 12.
  • In the settings file. The switch and the two steps marked done by hand travel in the settings file, and Reset to defaults turns the switch on again and clears the marks. See Move settings between orgs.
  • Archived so far. Under Purge runs, a line adds up the Intervals archived across the purge runs you can see, such as "8,090 Intervals archived so far, across 3 purge runs." It is read only on the Free plan. See Retention and purge.
  • Goal met counts only Intervals that had a Goal. An Interval in a value with no Goal is left out, so a value, owner, or period where none had a Goal shows a dash and is spoken as "No Interval had a Goal", not 100 percent. Each summary row now records how many of its Intervals had a Goal in Goal Count. After upgrading, run Rebuild summaries once over the months the charts read, because rows built before this version have no count and show a dash until then. See Build a dashboard.
  • Part weeks and part months on the Trend. A week or month the period covers only part of is marked "part week" or "part month" in its axis label, its tooltip, and its row in the table.
  • From and To in the zoom dialog. The full-screen view of a Trend has From and To selects, so a range can be set from the keyboard as well as by dragging.
  • Dashboards settings. The Tracked field select opens on a blank first choice, "The first Tracked field", and names the stored field only while it is still tracked.
  • Goals split by a second field. The list of fields offers only the fields you can read.
  • Settings import. The Tracked field in a Dashboards file is compared ignoring case, so a file that carries case.ownerid into an org that applies Case.OwnerId changes nothing. The words of each import row now come from custom labels.
  • The Case guide. Track Cases and open your first report now leaves Closed values empty, so Sojourn counts every case status marked Closed in Setup as closed.

docs.title: Sprint 13: the settings levers (30 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Values that do not count. On an object's Values tab, choose values of a Tracked field that open no Interval: the clock stops while a record is in one and starts again at the next counted value. Goals, reports, and the timeline leave them out. See The Values tab.
  • Value groups. Name groups of values, such as Backlog or Active; each Interval carries its value's group in Value Group, so reports and summaries can count a group as one. A group applies to Intervals that open after it is saved.
  • Timeline colours. Choose Tide, Harbor, Slate, or Mist for each value's segments on the timeline, or leave it on Automatic. Coral stays for a Breach and Lantern for the current Interval.
  • Only that the value changed. For a field whose values are private, Intervals can keep only the time in each value and leave the values blank. It cannot be chosen on the status field or the field Closed when reads.
  • Owner tracking. Track owners who are users and queues, users only, or queues only, and choose to keep one owner stay when a record moves between members of the same queue.
  • Records to track. Conditions on the Records tab choose which records get Intervals, such as Origin equals Web; a record that stops matching keeps its Intervals.
  • Business hours by record type. Each record type can use its own business hours, which win over the object's and lose to the record's own hours field.
  • Goals split by a second field. A goal for each value of a field such as Priority, beside the value's own goal; the most specific goal wins. See Set goals.
  • Retention per object. Each Tracked object can keep its Intervals for its own number of days, or everything, while the org keeps N days. See Retention and purge.
  • Health thresholds. The Health screen under Operations sets when the Health Monitor needs attention, when something is wrong, and when a job counts as late. See The Health Monitor.
  • Breaches now. A Sojourn widget for Lightning dashboards that lists the open Breaches as each viewer sees them. See Breaches now.
  • The timeline in App Builder. Show goal ticks and breach stripes turns the goal ticks and breach stripes on or off, and Show archived history chooses when the archive is offered. See The timeline.
  • The settings file carries every setting of this sprint, except retention per object, and each setting is checked and skipped on its own with its screen's words. See Move settings between orgs.
  • Capture Change in Flow Builder. The action's inputs sit in one Record change section, Record first and Prior record second.
  • Encrypted fields. The field picker marks a Tracked field your org encrypts with Shield Platform Encryption, since Intervals copy its values in plain text. See Encrypted fields.
  • Breach alerts. The breach alert template emails only an active owner or manager.
  • Backfill on large objects. History and Seed backfill run as a chain of steps over one set of records, so a large object backfills without the batch limits.
  • Reconcile. Every closed Interval of a deleted record is flagged in the same run, not only the first 2,000.
  • Sojourn Dashboards. A stored layout with a key Sojourn does not write stays in the list and does not open until it is saved again. See Build a dashboard.
  • Dashboards settings. A Sojourn Admin sets what a new dashboard opens on, how many owners, Trend values, and Longest open rows the charts show, what the print preview starts with, and the dashboard, chart, and summary row limits, on the Dashboards screen under Data. A lower limit stops adding and never removes. On the Plus plan; in the settings file and Reset to defaults. See Set what dashboards start with.
  • New guide pages. Scope and limits, and sections on merged records, encrypted fields, after a sandbox refresh, and the first steps after install.

docs.title: Sprint 14: Sojourn Dashboards (23 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Sojourn Dashboards. A new tab where each manager builds their own dashboards of where the time went: time in each value against its Goal, owners, Breaches, and the longest open stays. A dashboard is its owner's alone. On the Plus plan; on the Free plan the tab shows what it offers. See Build a dashboard.
  • Six charts. Number, Bars, Trend, Share, Heatmap, and Table; any chart's menu has Show as table for its numbers. The filters above the charts (Tracked object and field, a period of 7, 30, or 90 days, business or calendar hours, and an owner or everyone) apply to every chart and are kept with the dashboard.
  • Layout editor. Add, move, and resize charts on a snapping grid, with Undo, the keyboard, and each chart type's size limits; up to 20 dashboards of up to 20 charts each. Start from Support desk begins with ten charts.
  • Zoom and print. Expand opens one chart full screen, and on a Trend you drag across the chart to zoom into a range. Print a dashboard in black and white or colour, on A4 or Letter, with the data tables at the end if you choose.
  • The Sojourn Dashboards permission. In the Sojourn Admin and Sojourn Manager permission sets, with the new Sojourn Dashboard object. See Assign permission sets.
  • Totals for every owner. The Summaries job also writes rows that add up every owner, marked All Owners, so a chart for everyone reads one row a day. The packaged summary reports leave them out, so nothing is counted twice; a report of your own on Interval Summaries should filter All Owners equals false (see the report cookbook).
  • Summaries in parts of 1,000. The Summaries job and Rebuild summaries now count 1,000 Intervals at a time, so a night with many owners stays inside Salesforce's limits.

docs.title: Sprint 12: the settings console (23 October 2026)
docs.text:
• The Settings menu in four sections. Capture (Overview, Tracked objects), Time (Business hours, Goals, Alerts), Data (Retention and purge, Summaries, Export settings), and Operations (Jobs, Advanced), so each setting sits with its subject. The menu stays in view while a screen scrolls, in a console app too.
  • Jobs screen. The Jobs card moves off the Overview to its own screen under Operations, showing what it showed; the Overview keeps one line on how the jobs stand, with Open Jobs. See Run the jobs.
  • Run now. Each job's card starts one run of Live values, Reconcile, or Summaries straight away, as you, and leaves its schedule as it is. It is refused while that job is running, and when Salesforce already holds the most batch jobs it allows.
  • Live values window. Keep current for, on the Live values card, sets how many days back Live values keeps open Intervals current, from 1 to 365, 90 by default. It saves with Change or Turn on.
  • Alerts screen. The Breach alerts card moves off Goals, unchanged, to its own screen under Time. See Email a breach alert.
  • Summaries screen. Rebuild summaries moves here from Retention and purge, beside Roll-up: how many days Day rows are kept before only their Month rows remain, from 35 to 3,650, 400 by default. See Summaries.
  • Purge part size. Under Advanced on the Retention and purge screen's Purge card: how many Intervals each purge part saves to a file and deletes, from 50 to 2,000, 2,000 by default. On the Plus plan, with purge.
  • Which business hours an Interval uses. A card on the Business hours screen lists the order Sojourn applies: the Tracked field, the record's hours field, the queue, the object, then the Sojourn default.
  • Object screen in tabs. Fields, Records, Backfill, Live values, and Advanced, under the object's header. One Save on every tab saves all of them together, switching tabs keeps your changes, and a value that cannot be saved is named with its tab. See The object's tabs.
  • The object's Advanced tab. Lookup to fill on each Interval chooses which lookup Sojourn fills when two or more lookups on Interval point to the object. History backfill: records per chunk sets how many records a History backfill reads at a time, from 5 to 50, 20 by default, in the new History Chunk Size field on Tracked Object; on the Plus plan, with History backfill.
  • Advanced screen. The three limits Sojourn leaves in each save for your own automation (queries, rows, and CPU), and on the Plus plan the Omni-Channel statuses that start agent work, chosen from the org's list. Reset to defaults puts these, the Live values window, the purge part size, and the roll-up days back to their defaults after you type RESET; Tracked objects, fields, goals, retention, alerts, and job schedules are kept. See Tune the advanced settings.
  • Every setting names its default. Each number box shows the saved number, or the default while none is saved, and its hint names the default; a blank box goes back to it, and a number out of range is refused with what to enter. On the Free plan, the Plus settings show with their controls off and the Plus notice.
  • Usage. The Overview estimates the Intervals written this month, the storage Sojourn's records use and their share of your data storage, and a year at this rate, at 2 KB a row. See The Overview.
  • Links. The new screens and the object's tabs have their own links, and a link saved before opens the same card in its new place. The Health Monitor's job fixes open the Jobs screen and name it. See Links into Sojourn.
  • The settings file carries the new settings. Export settings now writes the Live values window, the three limits, the roll-up days, the Omni-Channel statuses, and each Tracked object's lookup to fill and History chunk, and the import checks each as its screen does. The purge part size stays in the org, with retention. See Move settings between orgs.
  • Salesforce API version 68.0. Every component of both packages is at API version 68.0 (Winter '27).

docs.title: Sprint 11: the live check fixes (20 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Closed when. Each Tracked object says when its records count as closed: the status field holds one of the closed values, or one checkbox on the record, such as IsClosed on Opportunity, is checked. The object screen lists every checkbox on the object as "Label (API name)", except Deleted. The choice is saved, exported, and imported with the object's other settings. See When a record closes.
  • Record Closed. While a record is closed, its Intervals carry the new Record Closed flag, and so does every Interval that opens before it reopens. The owner's stay ends at the close, and no Owner Interval opens while the record stays closed. A reopen starts a new owner stay for the owner the record has then. Capture, History and Seed backfill, Catch up, Reconcile, Live values, and the Case metrics all follow the same rule, and the nightly Reconcile puts the flag in step on the open Intervals of the records it checks.
  • Warning. An Interval whose business minutes reach its goal's warn percent is flagged Warning, with Warned At set to the moment it got there. Live values flags open Intervals, and a stay is flagged when it closes. A breached Interval is always a warning too. The Goals screen says what Warn at does, and the timeline names a warning in a stay's details. See Set goals.
  • Breach and warning times to the second. Breached At and Warned At count the goal from the second an Interval entered its value, not from the start of that minute, so under Business hours that close they are no longer up to a minute early. A goal that ran out at closing time had been stamped at the close; it now lands when the hours open again, at the seconds it entered with.
  • Value group and summary columns. Intervals gain Value Group, and Interval Summaries gain Value Group, Record Type, and Snapshot 1, each part of a summary row's key from the first version, and the report types show them. They stay blank for now; value groups come in sprint 13.
  • Links into Sojourn. Each Sojourn Settings screen, Tracked object, and card, and each Health Monitor tab and error status, has its own address. The address follows you as you move, so you can copy it at any time, and a link to an object that is not tracked opens Tracked objects and says so. See Links into Sojourn.
  • Reports and dashboards. The Lead and Opportunity reports average finished stays only, and the change counts per Case leave out Cases never tracked. Reports of open stays leave out closed records by Record Closed, and Longest Open Intervals lists the open stays entered longest ago. The weekly trend runs in date order. SLA Health counts breaches and open Cases and shows the hours to first close, and the dashboards chart counts, not sums, and hours, not minutes. The Case, Lead, and Opportunity report types list only records with Intervals, and the two by-Case reports open on Cases created in the last 30 days. Report types on Intervals show Record Closed, Warning, Warned At, and Value Group.
  • Weekly trends without closed time. Summary rows keep time spent while a record was closed apart, in a new Record Closed column of their own, and Average Hours per Status by Week leaves it out, so no Closed line runs through the weekly charts.
  • Owner changes per Case. A Case closed and reopened by the same owner no longer counts an owner change; only a different owner is a handoff.
  • Longest Open Intervals. A Days Open column gives every stay its calendar days to now, beside the business minutes Live values keeps for recent stays.
  • Imported records. A Case, Lead, or Opportunity imported with its original Created Date starts its first Intervals at that date, not at the import.
  • Deleted records. Reconcile flags every Interval of a deleted record, not only the ones still open, so reports that leave out orphaned Intervals leave out the whole record.
  • Undeleted records. A record brought back from the Recycle Bin is tracked again: its Intervals lose the orphaned flag and carry on from where they stopped. Only the Intervals Reconcile ended at the deletion open again, marked by a new Closed at Deletion checkbox; an owner stay that ended when the record closed, or agent work that had ended, stays ended. Summaries leave out an Interval Reconcile ended at the deletion for the 15 days the record can be brought back and one day more, so the next Reconcile can open it again: a reopened Interval is counted once, when it next closes, and one whose record stays deleted is counted after the 16 days. Reconcile finds records back from the Recycle Bin however many deleted records are still in it.
  • Repair of owner changes on closed records. Create interval resolves an owner change on a record that is closed, with the reason: owner time is not counted while a record is closed, so there is no Interval to create.
  • Rule owners on records created closed. A Case or Lead created closed and assigned by a rule in the same save takes the rule's owner on its first Intervals.
  • Field API names. The object screen shows each field's API name under its label, and the field lists read "Label (API name)", so two fields with the same label are told apart. On a window narrower than 1360 px, the Tracked fields list sits above the chosen fields instead of pushing the page sideways.
  • Intervals tab. Three list views, All Intervals, Open Intervals, and Breached Intervals, and an Interval page in sections (the value, the time, the goal, Live values, the record's snapshot) with read-only fields and highlights at the top.
  • Notifications. They sit over the Settings content, centred on it, just below the Salesforce header whatever its height. Pause, Resume, Turn on, Run backfill, Save settings, and the Overview's job buttons now say what they did, and Save settings keeps your choice on screen while the Overview reloads.
  • Loading and busy. The Tracked objects list loads under its real column labels, and Re-check Flows shows it is at work.
  • Retention. Neither choice is selected until you save one, and the org time zone is named once.
  • Repair. Create interval refuses, with the reason, an error that has no Interval to create; the nightly retries count it and stop after three, instead of looping.
  • Jobs card. Live values says how far back it keeps Intervals current (90 days unless changed), and each job's schedule is read from the job itself.
  • Warnings follow the Interval. Each new Interval carries its warn threshold as Warn Minutes beside Goal Minutes, so changing or turning off a goal no longer changes the warnings of Intervals already started, just as it leaves their Breach. Purge CSV files gain Warning and Warned at columns at the end, the archive keeps each Interval's warning, and summary rows count warnings in Warning Count.
  • Settings files. A file of more than 1,000,000 characters is refused before it is read, and the import box can be read again after an edit. A file with a misspelt setting is refused with Sojourn's own sentence alone.
  • Purge files and the archive keep what summaries group by. Purge CSV files gain Record Closed and Value Group columns after Warned at, and the archive keeps each Interval's Record Closed Flag and Value Group. See Keep or purge Intervals.
  • Open Intervals list view. It leaves out the Intervals of closed records and shows Calendar Minutes To Date, which is always current, in place of Exited At and Elapsed Business Hours, which stay empty until a stay ends.
  • Average Hours per Owner, 30 Days. It leaves out time spent while the Case was closed, as Average Hours per Status, 90 Days does. Share of Time per Status Group says in its description that its groups hold example statuses to edit.
  • Goals. Warn At Percent is refused outside 1 to 100 on every save, not only on the Goals screen and in a settings file.
  • Summary rows. A value, group, record type, or snapshot that contains a pipe no longer shares a summary row with another. Rows built before this change are recounted by Rebuild summaries.
  • Error messages. A failure Sojourn did not describe itself reaches Sojourn Settings, the Health Monitor, and the timeline as a fixed sentence that says what to do, never Salesforce's own words, which can name objects and fields. A save Salesforce refused still shows the reason it gave. Backfill, Catch up, Purge, and the nightly Summaries run report a failed part the same way, in their results and in the Error Log message, and so does a Flow check that could not read your Flows; Salesforce's own words stay in the error's technical details, which only Sojourn admins see. A Live values, Reconcile, or Summaries run with failed chunks says how many on the Jobs card and the Health Monitor, and Salesforce's reason stays in Setup, under Apex Jobs.
  • Read failures. When Reconcile's Recycle Bin check or the Error Log's record names cannot be read for a reason other than missing access, the failure is written to the Error Log instead of passing as no data. On the timeline, such a failure shows as an error instead of an empty history; a reader without access still sees what they may read.
  • Name field and snapshot fields. The object screen lists only fields you can read. The guide says which record values everyone with Sojourn User can read on Intervals, so you can choose a Name field to suit; see Add an object.

docs.title: Sprint 10: the last fixes before promotion (20 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Loading states. Every Sojourn Settings and Health Monitor screen shows a loading state shaped like its content until its data arrives, instead of an empty page.
  • Busy buttons. The button you press shows the Lanes mark at work until its action ends.
  • Notifications. What an action did appears at the top of the page as a slim Harbor bar, one stack each for Done, Started, and Failed, with the newest in front and a count that opens the list. Done and Started close after 6 seconds; point at one to read the whole message and keep it open. A failure says what went wrong and stays until you dismiss it. Repair results that list problems still show on their screen.
  • Partial saves. When a save of many records partly fails and Salesforce saves the rest again, each saved record keeps an Interval for every value it passed through in that save, including changes your own automation made in the same save.
  • Backfill. A backfill that cannot start, for example because its object is no longer tracked, shows Failed with the reason at once instead of staying Queued.

docs.title: Sprint 9 (in progress): review fixes and lock-in (20 October 2026)
docs.text:
What is merged so far; promoting the 1.0.0 packages and submitting them for the security review come after sprint 10.

  • Assignment rules. A Case or Lead that an assignment rule routes when it is created starts with the rule's owner, so its first queue time is right.
  • Breach at close. An Interval that closes past its goal is flagged as a Breach when it closes, not only by Live values. A new Breach alerts card on the Goals screen chooses whether owners are also emailed when a stay closes past its goal; it is off by default.
  • Correct Intervals in edge cases. A save that partly fails records every row that saves, Reconcile and Catch up open no blank or unchanged Intervals, and a record with two open Intervals for one field heals on its next change.
  • Health Monitor. Repair recomputes the Case figures as the person running it, errors carry stable codes, and no stack trace or query text reaches people who are not admins. The error list says when it shows only the newest 200.
  • Jobs say what they did. A backfill that a move to the Free plan cut short finishes Failed and says why, Purge now waits while summaries are rebuilt, and the object screen's Backfill card lists the last Catch up.
  • The Elapsed Business Hours and Elapsed Calendar Hours fields replace Business Hours and Calendar Hours on Intervals, so a duration is never confused with a Business hours schedule.
  • Numbers and months follow your locale, every field has a description and help text, and the install guide adds the step that sets each dashboard's running user.

docs.title: Sprint 8: Free and Plus plans, hardening, and performance runs (18 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Free and Plus plans. Sojourn installs on the Free plan: tracking Case, Lead, and Opportunity, the record timeline, the reports and dashboards, goals and breach flags, business hours, pause and Catch up, summaries, the Health Monitor, and settings export and import. The Plus plan adds tracking for any other object, Live values on the record, Backfill with History or Seed, purge and the archive, and Omni-Channel agent work. On Free, Plus features stay visible in Sojourn Settings with their controls off and an Upgrade to Plus link. Moving an org from Plus to Free deletes nothing. See Free and Plus plans.
  • New guide pages: Check the prerequisites, Track Cases and open your first report, Run the jobs, Troubleshooting, and Uninstall Sojourn. The install guide gains the upgrade steps, and Assign permission sets explains that Intervals are Public Read Only and how to make them Private.
  • Checks on every change: every Sojourn screen method checks a Sojourn permission before it reads or writes, production code has no test-only switches, no record Id is written into code or metadata, and only the ChangeCapture entry point is global.
  • Performance: 2,000 Cases loaded through Bulk API 2.0 with Status and owner tracked cost Sojourn about 400 ms of CPU per 200-record chunk, and summaries, reconcile, and purge were timed on 72,003 Intervals. The results are in Reports at large volume.

docs.title: Sprint 7: the record timeline, reports, and dashboards (14 October 2026)
docs.text:
• The Sojourn Timeline on record pages and Experience Cloud pages: a lane per Tracked field, each stay sized by its time, goal ticks and the time past a goal, details on focus or hover, and totals by value and by owner. History purged to the archive shows too, marked as archived.
  • The Sojourn Timeline permission, in the Sojourn User, Manager, Health Monitor, and Admin permission sets, and a new Sojourn Site User permission set for Experience Cloud users. The timeline shows the history of a record only to people who can open the record.
  • 20 reports in the Sojourn Reports folder and 4 dashboards in Sojourn Dashboards: Desk Productivity, Process Bottlenecks, SLA Health, and Leaderboards. Trends and leaderboards read the daily summaries, so they stay fast at any volume.
  • The report cookbook gains worked examples, hours per Case, status groups, and reports at large volume, and the reference lists every report and dashboard with the filters it relies on.
  • Live values, goals, and capture use the same status field as the Case metrics when an object has none chosen.

docs.title: Sprint 6: Case metrics, Omni-Channel, and breach alerts (13 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Case metrics on every Case: first closed at, business minutes to first close, reopens, owner and status changes, and business minutes held by queues, by agents, and in total. They are rebuilt from the Case's own Intervals whoever saves the Case, and by Backfill and repair.
  • The Sojourn Omni-Channel package: one Agent work Interval per agent assignment of routed work, closed with its minutes when the work ends. It installs only in orgs with Omni-Channel; the core package does not need it.
  • The Sojourn Breach Alert Template Flow: save a copy, activate it, and the Interval owner and their manager get one email when an Interval breaches its goal.
  • The Case Status At Close field on Intervals is removed before the first release.
  • The purge runs list shows how many files each run saved, and a stopped run shows what it deleted before it stopped.

docs.title: Sprint 5: summaries, retention, goals, and moving settings (12 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Summaries each night: closed Intervals counted into daily and monthly rows, kept when Intervals are purged, with the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type and Rebuild summaries for whole months.
  • Retention and purge: choose Keep everything or Keep a number of days. A purge deletes only closed, summarised Intervals older than the window, saves each part to a CSV file on its purge run first, and can copy them to the archive. Purge now runs one straight away; both ask you to type DELETE.
  • Goals per value of a Tracked field, in business minutes, with a warn-at percent.
  • Business hours per queue, so time owned by a queue counts in that queue's hours.
  • Export settings to a file and import it in another org, with a check of what will change before Apply, and Replace what is here to match the file.
  • At most 10 Tracked fields per object, Start timing at the first value for fields that start blank, and an Estimate of the Interval rows and storage your choice adds.
  • The Sojourn app has three tabs: Sojourn Settings, Health Monitor, and Intervals.
  • The Health Monitor shows a Flow you cannot see as information rather than a warning, and a catch up keeps its window when capture was paused during the run.

docs.title: Sprint 4: jobs and the Health Monitor (12 October 2026)
docs.text:
• Backfill from an object's screen: History builds past Intervals from field history, Seed starts each record from its current values, and Fresh starts with the next change. The card shows Queued, Running, Complete, or Failed with what was done.
  • Catch up after a pause: the records changed while capture was paused get their Intervals at the time they changed, and running it again is safe.
  • Live values: minutes to date and breach flags on open Intervals, and the minute fields on each record, every 10, 15, 20, 30, or 60 minutes.
  • Reconcile each night: flags Intervals of deleted or merged records, repairs drift from the record's current values, and retries Limit and DML errors.
  • A Jobs card on the Sojourn Settings overview to turn Live values and Reconcile on, change their schedule, and see the last and next run.
  • The Health Monitor tab: overall health, capture checks, job runs, error counts, and an error list with Create Interval, Ignore, and Mark resolved, each error with what happened, why, and how to fix it.
  • The Sojourn Health Monitor permission set, so a support or operations group can fix errors without Sojourn Settings.
  • Tracking errors are now the Error Log, with a Create Interval action on each record.
  • The Sojourn Settings screens match the approved designs, and the Tracked objects list shows each object's Tracked fields, Track owner, and where its business hours come from.

docs.title: Sprint 3: Flow template and Sojourn Settings (12 October 2026)
docs.text:
• The Sojourn Settings page, with a Sojourn menu that folds into icons and remembers the choice.
  • Add any object Sojourn can track from a searchable list, with no API names to type.
  • Choose Tracked fields, Track owner, status field and closed values, name field, business hours, up to five snapshot fields, record types, and Live values fields on one screen.
  • Pause and Resume capture per object, with the time the pause started.
  • A capture status for every Tracked object: Tracked by package, Flow active, Flow missing, or Flow unknown, with Re-check.

docs.title: Report cookbook
docs.text: Tell us the report you need and we will write it up first.

docs.title: Filter by object, then field, then value
docs.text:
Every interval belongs to one Tracked object and one Tracked field. Before you group by Value, filter or group by Tracked object and then Tracked field. A grouping that mixes fields adds Status minutes to Owner minutes, and the totals stop meaning anything.

The 19 packaged reports (20 with Sojourn Omni-Channel) and 4 dashboards, with the filters each relies on, are listed in Reports and dashboards. They follow this rule: each filters Tracked Field before it groups by value. The dashboards run as the user each one names, the installing admin until you change it; see step 3 of Install Sojourn before you share them.

docs.title: Average finished stays only
docs.text:
An open stay has no business minutes until it ends, so its Elapsed Business Hours is 0, and an average that takes in open stays runs low. Every packaged report that averages hours filters Exited At not blank; do the same in your own reports. For the time so far on open stays, use Business Minutes To Date, which the Live values job keeps current for the stays entered within its window; older open stays show it blank.

For open stays of any age, Longest Open Intervals has a Days Open column: a row-level formula, Calendar Minutes To Date divided by 1,440, with one decimal place. It is current on every row, because Calendar Minutes To Date counts to now for an open stay, and it counts calendar days, not business hours. To add it to your own report, choose Add Row-Level Formula, type Number, insert Calendar Minutes To Date from the field list, and divide it by 1440.

In the same way as the hours averages, Status Changes per Case and Owner Changes per Case filter their counts not blank, so Cases that were never tracked do not average in as zero.

docs.title: Leave closed records out of open stays
docs.text:
A record's last Interval stays open after the record closes: a closed Case sits in an open Closed stay. Sojourn checks Record Closed on the Intervals of a record while it is closed, by the Tracked object's closed setting. The reports of open stays, Open Cases by Status and Time to Date and Longest Open Intervals, and the Open Intervals list view on the Intervals tab filter Open true and Record Closed false. Average Hours per Status, 90 Days and Average Hours per Owner, 30 Days leave out the time reopened Cases spent closed. The Open Intervals list view shows Calendar Minutes To Date, which is always current; Elapsed Business Hours stays empty until a stay ends.

The dashboards chart hours or counts, never minutes: SLA Health counts breaches and open Cases, and shows the hours to first close.

  • Worked examples: time in status for a queue, time per owner, and the statuses that miss their goal.
  • Hours per Case: total business hours, from the Case metrics or from the Intervals.
  • Status groups: report time by value group, or edit the bucket that splits customer time from company time.
  • Reports at large volume: date ranges, custom indexes, and summaries for trends.

docs.title: Report on summaries
docs.text:
Summary rows keep the totals after Intervals are purged; see Keep or purge Intervals. Use the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type.

  1. Filter Granularity to Month for trends, or Day for the last weeks. Never add Day and Month rows together: each Month row already holds its days.
  2. Filter All Owners to False. Rows with All Owners true add up every owner's rows for the same day or month, for Sojourn Dashboards; adding both counts each Interval twice. The packaged summary reports already filter it.
  3. Filter Parent Object and Tracked Field, as for Intervals, then group by To Value, and by Owner Name for time per owner.
  4. For the average time in a value, add a summary formula: the sum of Sum Business Minutes divided by the sum of Interval Count. Averaging Avg Business Minutes across rows weighs a quiet day like a busy one.
  5. Breach Count counts the Intervals that ran past their goal, and Warning Count the Intervals that reached their goal's warn percent. A Breach is also a warning, so for goals with a warn percent, Warning Count less Breach Count is the stays that came close and finished in time. Goal Count counts the Intervals that had a goal when they started, so the sum of Breach Count over the sum of Goal Count is the breach rate of the stays with a goal, leaving out values that have none.

Record Count is close, not exact. It counts each record once per row as the row is built. A record that gets another Interval later for a period already summarised is counted again on that row, so the count can run slightly high. Interval Count and the minutes are exact.

docs.title: Merged and deleted records
docs.text:
When records are merged, Salesforce deletes the records merged away, and their Intervals keep their own Parent Id and Parent Name: Sojourn does not move them onto the record that remains. The next Reconcile closes their open stays and checks Orphaned on each; see When records are merged.

  • In the Sojourn Intervals report type, a merged record's stays show apart from the record that remains. Filter Orphaned to False to count only records that still exist, or leave the filter off to keep every stay in the totals.
  • A merge moves related records to the record that remains, so a report type that starts from the record, such as Leads with Sojourn Intervals, lists the merged record's stays under the remaining record. Filter Orphaned to False to leave them out once Reconcile has run; before then, add Parent Id to the report, since a merged stay keeps the Id of the record merged away.
  • Summary rows count stays by value and owner, so the merged record's stays stay in their totals. A stay that Reconcile closed at the merge is counted once 16 days have passed, as for any deleted record; see Run the jobs.

docs.title: Opportunity amounts in more than one currency
docs.text: Opportunity Amount on an Interval is the Opportunity's Amount when the stay began, in the Opportunity's own currency, with no conversion. In an org with more than one currency, a sum or average of it across Opportunities adds amounts in different currencies, so the total means nothing. Report on Opportunities in one currency at a time, or take converted amounts from your own Opportunity reports.

docs.title: Email me when Sojourn logs an error
docs.text:
Sojourn writes an Error Log row whenever it cannot record a change or a job cannot run. To hear about it without opening the Health Monitor, subscribe to a copy of the packaged Error Log by Type report. You need the Sojourn Admin or Sojourn Health Monitor permission set to read Error Log rows, and Salesforce's Subscribe to Reports permission.

  1. Open Reports, then the Sojourn Reports folder, then Error Log by Type. Choose Save As, give the copy a name such as Sojourn errors to fix, and save it in a folder of your own.
  2. Edit the copy, add the filter Status equals New, and save it. The report now lists only the errors that need you.
  3. Choose Subscribe. Set the schedule to Daily, at a time early in your working day.
  4. Under Run Report As, choose a user with Sojourn Admin or Sojourn Health Monitor, so the report sees every Error Log row. Every recipient sees what that user sees, messages included, and a message can hold a record's values, so add only people who may read them.
  5. Add a condition: Record Count, greater than, 0. Then choose Save.

The email now arrives only on the mornings when at least one error waits. Fix each one from the Health Monitor; see Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor.

docs.title: From the Case metrics
docs.text:
Every Case carries Sojourn Total Business Minutes: the business minutes it spent with finished owners, queues and users together. See Read the Case metrics.

  1. Create a report on the standard Cases report type.
  2. Add Sojourn Total Business Minutes, Sojourn Queue Business Minutes, and Sojourn Agent Business Minutes.
  3. For hours, add a summary formula: the sum of Sojourn Total Business Minutes divided by 60.

The time with the current owner is not in these totals until the owner changes; it is in Sojourn Owner Minutes while Live values run.

docs.title: From the Intervals
docs.text:
1. Open Time in Status by Case and Save As. It opens on Cases created in the last 30 days; change the date range for older Cases.
  2. Remove the grouping by To Value, so each Case shows one line.
  3. Elapsed Business Hours summed per Case is the time in every status the Case has left. The current, open stay counts 0 until it ends; its time so far is Business Minutes To Date, kept by the Live values job.

Use one way per report: the two count the current stay differently.

docs.title: Reports at large volume
docs.text:
An org that tracks several fields on busy objects writes Intervals quickly. These habits keep reports fast.

  1. Filter on a date range of Entered At. Every Interval report should limit Entered At, or the report's own date, to the weeks you need. The packaged averages already look back 30 or 90 days, and Time in Status by Case and Time per Owner by Case open on Cases created in the last 30 days.
  2. Ask Salesforce Support for custom indexes on Entered_At__c, Tracked_Field__c, and Parent_Object__c of Sojourn Intervals once the object passes a few million rows. Support adds custom indexes on request.
  3. Use the daily summaries for trends. Average Hours per Status by Week and Owner Leaderboard, Last 30 Days read the Interval Summaries, one row per day, value, and owner, so they stay fast at any volume. The packaged dashboards' trend and leaderboard charts read only these. In Average Hours per Status by Week, a week runs from Sunday and is named by that date (2026-07-19), so the chart's labels stay short and in date order. See Report on summaries.
  4. Keep detail off on large groupings. Summary reports with Show Details off return totals without every row.

Often missed. Purging old Intervals keeps the summaries. Trends built on summaries survive a purge; reports on Intervals show only what is left. See Keep or purge Intervals.

docs.title: What we measured
docs.text:
A scratch org holding 6,000 Cases and 72,003 Intervals spread over 400 days, on the Plus plan, gave these times in sprint 8:

Step Result The 19 Sojourn reports All ran; the slowest took 4 seconds, the rest 1 second or less Summaries 72,003 Intervals counted in 81 seconds Reconcile 7 seconds Purge, keeping 30 days 57,715 Intervals saved to CSV files and deleted in 231 seconds, no errors

Loading 2,000 Cases through Bulk API 2.0 with Status and owner tracked cost Sojourn about 400 ms of CPU per 200-record chunk; each chunk's whole save stayed under 600 ms. A scratch org holds far fewer Intervals than a production org, so the same steps run again at millions of Intervals in a sandbox before Sojourn is listed on AppExchange.

docs.title: Status groups
docs.text: Time waiting on the customer against time with your company is a question about groups of statuses, not single values. Sojourn answers it in two ways: value groups, which you set once and every Interval carries, and the Status group bucket in one packaged report.

docs.title: Report by value group
docs.text:
Value groups are set per Tracked field on the object's Values tab (see The Values tab). Each new Interval of the field carries its value's group in Value Group, and the summary rows keep each group apart, so a report can count Waiting on Customer and Waiting on Vendor as one Waiting group without a bucket.

  1. Open the Sojourn app and the Sojourn Settings tab, then Tracked objects, the object, and its Values tab. Choose the field, such as Status, and under Value groups select Add a group. Name it, for example Customer, and add its values. Add the other groups the same way, then Save.
  2. Create a report on the Sojourn Intervals report type. Filter Parent Object and Tracked Field, as for every Interval report, and Exited At not blank, so open stays do not lower the average.
  3. Group the rows by Value Group. Add the sum and the average of Elapsed Business Hours, and the record count.

For trends over months, or after a purge, use the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type instead: filter Granularity, All Owners to False, Parent Object, and Tracked Field as in Report on summaries, group by Value Group, and take the sum of Sum Business Minutes divided by the sum of Interval Count for the average.

Often missed. A group applies to the Intervals opened after you save it. Earlier Intervals, and values in no group, show Value Group blank, and a report lists them as a blank group. Rebuild summaries counts Intervals as they are stored, so it does not move earlier stays into a new group.

docs.title: Edit the packaged bucket
docs.text:
Share of Time per Status Group sums business minutes per status group with a bucket field named Status group, which works on Intervals written before you set value groups too. The package cannot know your status values, so the report ships with example values:

Group Example statuses Customer Waiting on Customer Company New, Working, Escalated Other Every status not listed

Until you edit the bucket, an org whose statuses have other names sees every stay in Other.

  1. Open Share of Time per Status Group and select Save As into your folder.
  2. In the report builder, open the Status group column's menu and select Edit Bucket Column.
  3. Move each of your statuses into Customer or Company, add groups if you need them, and save.

A report has at most 5 bucket fields, 20 buckets per field, and 20 values per bucket.

You are done when a report grouped by Value Group, or the saved copy of Share of Time per Status Group, shows your groups with the hours you expect for a Case you know.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text: Each example starts from a packaged report in Sojourn Reports. Packaged reports are read only: select Save As to keep your changes in your own folder. The sample results below come from a demo org.

docs.title: Where did this queue's Cases spend their time this month?
docs.text:
1. Open Time in Status by Case, then Save As into your folder. It lists Cases with at least one Interval, created in the last 30 days.
  2. In Filters, add Case Owner equals your queue, and set the date range to This Month on Date/Time Opened.
  3. Keep the filter Tracked Field equals Status: it is what keeps Status time apart from Owner time.
Case Status Business hours 00001027 Working 10.25 00001027 Waiting on Customer 9.00 00001027 Escalated 2.50 00001031 New 0.75 00001031 Working 4.00

docs.title: Who held a Case, and for how long?
docs.text:
1. Open Time per Owner by Case. Like Time in Status by Case, it opens on Cases created in the last 30 days; widen the date range for an older Case.
  2. Filter Case Number to the Case, or keep every Case and sort by Elapsed Business Hours.
  3. Queues and users both appear; a queue's time counts in that queue's business hours (see Set goals and business hours).
Case Owner Business hours 00001027 Tier 1 1.50 00001027 Priya Shah 12.00 00001027 Tier 2 2.00 00001027 Marco Diaz 7.00

docs.title: Which statuses miss their goal most often?
docs.text:
1. Open SLA Breaches by Status and Owner. It lists every stay that went past its Goal, by value and then owner.
  2. To see one object, add Parent Object equals Case.
  3. Breaches are flagged by the Live values job; see Track an object.
  4. Business hours adds up the stays that ended: a breach still open counts as one breach and 0 hours. The SLA Health dashboard charts the number of breaches, so open ones show.
Status Owner Breaches Business hours Working Priya Shah 3 19.50 Working Marco Diaz 1 6.25 New Tier 1 2 3.00

docs.title: Which stays are close to their goal?
docs.text:
1. Create a report on the Sojourn Intervals report type (or Cases with Sojourn Intervals).
  2. Filter Warning equals True and Breached equals False: the stays that reached their goal's warn percent but not the goal itself.
  3. Add Open equals True to see only the stays still running, and group by To Value and Owner Name.
  4. Warned At is when each stay reached the warn percent. Open stays are flagged by the Live values job and closed ones when they close; see Set goals and business hours.

docs.title: Tune the advanced settings
docs.text: Most orgs never change these. Open Sojourn Settings, then Advanced under Operations. Each setting names its default, and a blank box always means the default, so an org that never opens this screen runs as Sojourn ships. Changing a setting needs the Customize Application permission, as the Overview settings do.

docs.title: Limits in a save
docs.text:
Sojourn records Intervals inside your users' saves, so it shares each save's Salesforce limits with your own triggers, Flows, and other apps: in a user's save, 100 queries, 10,000 rows written, and 10 seconds of CPU time. Before it does its work, Sojourn checks that the save would still have this much left over for everything else. When it would not, Sojourn steps aside: it writes a Limit error to the Error Log instead of the Interval, the user's save goes through, and the nightly Reconcile retries the change. See Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor.

Setting What it leaves for your automation Default Range Queries left for your automation Queries the save can still run 10 1 to 50 Rows left for your automation Rows the save can still insert, update, or delete 2,000 100 to 5,000 CPU left for your automation, milliseconds CPU time the save can still spend 2,000 500 to 9,000

A higher number leaves more for your automation, and Sojourn steps aside sooner, so more changes wait for Reconcile; a lower number does the opposite. None of them can be 0, so Sojourn never spends the last of a limit. Rows stop at 5,000 because that is the most one Summaries chunk writes, so a larger reserve would leave room no job uses. A number saved outside its range some other way, for example by editing Sojourn's custom setting in Setup, is read as the nearest end of the range. Sojourn reads only the custom setting's org-wide values: a value set for a profile or a user in Setup has no effect, so no one can change, for their own saves, what Sojourn records about them.

Each box shows the saved number, or the default while none is saved. Clear a box to go back to its default, then choose Save limits. A number outside its range is refused, for example "Queries left for your automation: enter a whole number from 1 to 50, or leave it blank for the default, 10.", and nothing is saved.

docs.title: Omni-Channel
docs.text:
The Omni-Channel card shows when Omni-Channel is turned on in the org, whether or not the Sojourn Omni-Channel package is installed; without the package, the statuses you save record nothing. Agent work starts at lists the Agent Work statuses at which the Sojourn Omni-Channel package opens an Agent work Interval: Assigned and Opened unless you change them. Choose statuses from the org's own list, at least one, and choose Save statuses. Omni-Channel agent work is on the Plus plan, so on the Free plan the card shows the statuses with its controls off and the Plus notice.

The limits of Sojourn Dashboards, how many dashboards each person keeps, how many charts a dashboard holds, and how many summary rows one chart adds up, are under Advanced on the Dashboards screen. See Set what dashboards start with.

docs.title: Reset to defaults
docs.text:
Reset to defaults puts twenty-five settings back to their defaults: the four on this screen, six on other screens, the thirteen on the Dashboards screen, and the two of the Get started guide. The dialog names them as their screens do:

  • Live values: keep current for (days), on the Jobs screen
  • Queries left for your automation
  • Rows left for your automation
  • CPU left for your automation, milliseconds
  • Intervals per purge part, under Retention and purge (see The purge part size)
  • Day rows become Month rows after (days), on Summaries
  • Needs attention when open errors are more than, on the Health screen
  • Something is wrong when open errors are more than, on the Health screen
  • A job is late after (hours), on the Health screen
  • Agent work starts at
  • The thirteen Dashboards settings, on the Dashboards screen: New dashboard Tracked field, New dashboard period (days), New dashboard hours, Owners in an owner chart, Owners in the Owner filter, Values in a Trend, Rows in Longest open, Print in colour, Print paper, Print without data tables, Dashboards for each person, Charts on a dashboard, and Summary rows one chart adds up
  • The two Get started settings, on Get started: Guide Opens First is turned back on, so Sojourn Settings opens on the guide again while a required step remains, and Guide Marked Done is cleared, so the two steps marked done by hand show To do again

Tracking enabled, the default business hours, the retention period and the archive, Breach alerts, the job schedules, and every Tracked object, Tracked field, and goal are kept.

  1. Choose Reset to defaults. The dialog lists the twenty-five settings.
  2. Type RESET in capitals. Reset to defaults in the dialog turns on only when the word matches.
  3. Choose Reset to defaults. A notice says "Advanced settings are back to their defaults."

You are done when

  • Each box on the Advanced screen shows the number you saved, or its default, and its hint names the default.
  • After a reset, the Live values window on the Jobs screen reads 90 days again, and the Health screen shows its defaults.

docs.title: Backfill past Intervals
docs.text: A new Tracked object starts with the next change. Backfill gives the records that already exist their Intervals, so reports cover the time before you turned tracking on.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
Open Sojourn Settings, then Tracked objects, then the object, and its Backfill tab. The Backfill card offers three modes:

  • History recreates past Intervals from the object's field history: from each record's creation to its first change, then each change to the next, with the last one open. A Tracked field without history starts from its current value.
  • Seed starts each record from its current value: one open Interval per Tracked field, from the record's last change; the owner's Interval starts at the record's creation. A blank field set to Start timing at the first value gets no Interval from Seed, nor from Create interval on the Health Monitor: its first Interval opens when it first gets a value.
  • Fresh adds nothing: capture begins with the next change.

History and Seed are on the Plus plan; on the Free plan the card offers Fresh. See Free and Plus plans.

History and Seed give Intervals only to the records the object tracks: of a record type the object lists, when it lists any, and meeting its records to track (both set on the Records tab, see Track an object). They follow the object's owner tracking as capture does: under Users only a queue's stretch in the history is no owner Interval and the next user's stay continues the sequence, and with Ignore a move between members of the same queue a move between two direct members keeps one stay (see Track an object).

History needs field history tracking turned on for the object and its fields in Salesforce Setup before the changes happened. If the object keeps no field history at all, History seeds every record and says so in the result.

For the Closed when rule (see Track an object), History reads the field that decides: the status field, or the chosen checkbox. Track that field's history too. Without it, a closed record counts as closed since its last change, so its owner stay ends and Record Closed starts there rather than at the real close. A checkbox that Salesforce sets from the status, such as Closed (IsClosed) on Case and Opportunity, keeps no field history at all, so History always places its close at the last change. To run History on those objects, leave the Closed Checkbox Field empty and let the Closed values decide: Status and Stage keep history.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
1. Choose the mode, then Run backfill.
  2. Read the confirmation: it names the mode and the object. Choose Run backfill again.
  3. The card shows Queued, then Running, then Complete or Failed with what was done, for example "Seed backfill on 12 Oct 2026, 13:56: 60 Intervals for 20 records."

Run backfill is refused, with the reason, and nothing starts:

  • when the object is turned off: "Turn on Case first." A History or Seed run on an object Sojourn cannot read as a Tracked object, for example one that no longer exists in the org, is refused with its name and "is not tracked now."
  • for History or Seed on the Free plan.
  • while a backfill job is really running in the org (on any object) and this object's card says Queued or Running: "A backfill is still running. Try again when it finishes."
  • while a Catch up runs, and, for History and Seed, when Salesforce already holds 100 batch jobs (see Run the jobs).

The job runs as you: only records and fields you can see are read and written. A backfill and a Catch up never run at the same time: each is refused while the other runs, so their chunks cannot both open an Interval for the same field. Catch up and Seed leave alone a field that keeps only the change (see The Values tab): they cannot tell that its value changed.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
History and Seed run in the background as a chain of short jobs, one after another, not as one batch job. Each job reads its records in chunks and, while Salesforce's limits for that job leave room for another chunk, reads the next; then it starts the next job of the chain, which carries on from the next record. A chunk is 20 records for History and 200 for Seed, because History reads every field change of each record; the last chunk reads only the records left. Setup's Apex Jobs lists each job of the chain as a Queueable job of BackfillChain.

To change how many records a History chunk reads, set History backfill: records per chunk on the object's Advanced tab, from 5 to 50, and choose Save; fewer suit records with long field history. It is the size of every chunk except the last, and Salesforce's limits decide how many chunks one job of the chain runs, so a job with heavy records runs fewer of them. The chunk size is on the Plus plan, with History, and applies to the next run.

A run that stops part-way shows Failed with the records it finished, for example "History backfill on 23 Oct 2026, 12:23 stopped after 400 records: Salesforce stopped one link of the run, for example at a governor limit; see the Error Log. Records already done are skipped when you run it again." It stops that way when one job of the chain ends at a Salesforce limit, or when Salesforce does not start the next job, and the Error Log gets one row saying so. Salesforce keeps the run's list of records for 48 hours, so a run that has not finished by then stops at its next chunk, saying "Salesforce could no longer read the run's list of records, which it keeps for 48 hours; see the Error Log."; run it again to finish the rest. It also stops at its next job if the object stops being tracked, saying the object is not tracked now, and before its next chunk if the org leaves the Plus plan, saying how many chunks it did not run; run it again on Plus to finish. A Queued or Running backfill with no job left going, for example after a job was stopped in Setup, also shows Failed and says it stopped before it finished; you can run it again.

Very large objects. When you choose Run backfill, Sojourn lists the object's records once, as an Apex cursor the whole run reads from, so the confirmation can take a moment on an object with millions of records. Salesforce charges every record in that list to the org's daily allowance of Apex cursor rows: 100 million rows over a rolling 24 hours, for the whole org, shared with your own code and other apps. A backfill of an object with 20 million records uses a fifth of it. If your own code uses Apex cursors, spread the backfills of very large objects over more than one day. Run backfill is the only part of Sojourn that uses the allowance.

Safe to run again. Records and fields that already have Intervals are skipped, so a second run adds nothing to them. After a Failed run, run it again to finish the rest; the Error Log says what stopped it.

You are done when

  • The Backfill card reads Complete.
  • An Interval report on the object shows Intervals that start before you added it.

docs.title: Email a breach alert
docs.text: When an Interval runs past its goal, Sojourn marks it as breached: the Live values job marks an Interval that is still open, and a stay that closes past its goal before the job saw it is marked when it closes. The Sojourn Breach Alert Template Flow turns that moment into an email to the Interval's owner and, when they have one in Salesforce, their manager. It ships inactive, so nothing is sent until you choose to.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Flows, then Sojourn Breach Alert Template, and choose Save As, a new Flow.
  2. Change the subject and the body if you like. They name the record, the Tracked field, the value, the goal, and the business minutes so far.
  3. Activate your copy.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• For an open Interval, the alert fires inside the Live values job, which sets the breach. Schedule the Live values job on the Jobs screen of Sojourn Settings, under Operations; without it, open Intervals are not marked breached and no alert is sent for them. Run now on its card flags them at once. See Run the jobs.
  • By default the template emails only while an Interval is still open, when someone can still act. To email for a stay that closed past its goal too, open Sojourn Settings, then Alerts under Time, turn on Also email when a stay closes past its goal on the Breach alerts card, and choose Save. When to turn it on, on the card, explains the choice. The setting applies to every Tracked object; the breach flag and reports are the same either way.
  • Only Intervals owned by a user are alerted. Queue-owned Intervals have no user to email.
  • Only active users get the email. A record owned by an inactive user sends no alert, and when the owner's manager is inactive, the owner alone gets it. A copy you saved from an earlier version of the template keeps its own steps: save a new copy, or add Active Equals True to the Get Owner and Get Manager conditions of yours.
  • Each email counts toward the org's daily email limit. If an email cannot be sent, the Flow ends without it and the save that marked the breach carries on.
  • The email names the record and the value it is in, and the manager receives it whether or not they can open the record. If your record names are private, take the name out of the subject and body in your copy.
  • Your copy is yours to change: add a condition on the Tracked field, or send to a team address instead.

You are done when

  • An Interval owned by you passes its goal and, after the next Live values run, you receive the alert.

docs.title: Add Breaches now to a dashboard
docs.text: Breaches now is a widget for Lightning dashboards. It lists one Tracked object's open Intervals in Breach, the longest past its goal first, and, if you choose, the open Intervals At risk: those that reached their goal's warn percent. Each row links to the record, where the timeline is. Sojourn's four packaged dashboards do not carry it; you add it to a dashboard of your own, such as a copy of SLA Health.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
• Breaches. Each row is one open Interval past its goal: the record, its value, its owner, and how long it is past the goal in business hours, as the timeline counts it. A Coral mark starts each row. The line under the title counts them, as in "Case · 3 open past their goal".
  • At risk. With Show at risk on, a second group lists open Intervals that reached their warn percent but are not yet in Breach, with how much of the goal they have used, as in "85% of goal". A Lantern mark starts each row.
  • Live, with its own Refresh. The widget reads the Intervals when the dashboard opens. The dashboard's Refresh does not reach it, so it has its own Refresh button and its own "As of" time.
  • Flags from Live values. Sojourn marks an open Interval in Breach or At risk on each Live values run, so a stay that just passed its goal shows after the next run. See Run the jobs.

docs.title: Who can add it
docs.text: You need Run Reports and Create and Customize Dashboards in Salesforce. To pick a Tracked object you also need a Sojourn permission set that reads the Sojourn configuration: Sojourn Admin, Sojourn Manager, or Sojourn Health Monitor. Sojourn User alone does not; see Assign permission sets.

docs.title: Add it
docs.text:
1. Open a Lightning dashboard you own and select Edit.
  2. Select + Widget, then Lightning Web Component, then Breaches now.
  3. Set its properties, then select Add and Save.
Property What it does Tracked object The Tracked object whose open Intervals the widget lists. The list holds your active Tracked objects. Rows How many Breaches to show, from 1 to 20, the longest past its goal first. The default is 5. Show at risk Also lists open Intervals that reached their goal's warn percent (Warning), with the same Rows limit.

Often missed. The Tracked object list is read as you, the dashboard's author: without one of those permission sets it is empty. The editor shows at most 200 values.

docs.title: Each viewer sees their own records
docs.text: The widget always runs as the person viewing the dashboard, whatever the dashboard's running user. It lists only records that person can open, and it needs the Sojourn Timeline permission, which the Sojourn User, Manager, Health Monitor, and Admin permission sets include. The dashboard's other widgets show the data of its running user, so the two can count differently on the same dashboard. The widget also ignores the dashboard's filters.

docs.title: What Salesforce does not support
docs.text:
• One custom component per dashboard. A Lightning dashboard holds at most one Lightning web component widget, so Breaches now takes that place.
  • View Dashboard As. Salesforce does not support View Dashboard As on a dashboard that holds a Lightning web component.
  • Subscription emails. Salesforce leaves Lightning web component widgets out of dashboard subscription emails.

docs.title: When the widget is empty
docs.text:
The widget says What to do No open Case is past its goal Nothing to act on. Rows appear when an open stay passes its goal and Live values next runs. You need the Sojourn Timeline permission to see Breaches Assign the viewer a Sojourn permission set that includes it. Choose a Tracked object for this widget in the dashboard editor Edit the dashboard and choose a Tracked object. An object no longer tracked shows this too.

You are done when

  • The dashboard shows Breaches now with its Refresh button and "As of" time.
  • A viewer with the Sojourn User permission set sees the open records they can open that are past their goal, each linked to its record.

docs.title: Read the Case metrics
docs.text: Once Case is a Tracked object with Status tracked, and Track owner on for the owner figures, every Case carries eight figures that Sojourn keeps from the Case's own Intervals.

docs.title: The fields
docs.text:
Field What it holds Sojourn First Closed At When the Case first entered a closed status. Reopening does not change it. Sojourn First Close Business Minutes Business minutes in every status before that first close. Sojourn Reopen Count Times the Case moved from a closed status back to an open one. Sojourn Status Change Count Status changes after creation: the Case's Status Intervals minus one. Sojourn Owner Change Count Handoffs between owners: the Owner Intervals minus one. A Case never reassigned shows 0. Sojourn Queue Business Minutes Business minutes the Case spent owned by queues. Sojourn Agent Business Minutes Business minutes the Case spent owned by users. Sojourn Total Business Minutes Queue and agent minutes together.

The queue, agent, and total minutes count finished ownership only. Time with the current owner is in Sojourn Owner Minutes, which the Live values job keeps current on the Plus plan (see Track an object).

A status is closed when it is in the Tracked object's Closed values. With Closed values empty and Status as the status field, Sojourn uses the case statuses marked Closed in Setup. If you track a custom status field, list its closed values; otherwise no value counts as closed and the first-close figures stay blank. When the Tracked object names a Closed Checkbox Field, the first close and the reopens come from that checkbox's own Intervals instead, so track the checkbox as a field too (see When a record closes). The owner's minutes stop at each close: no Owner Interval is open while the Case is closed.

A status that does not count, set on the object's Values tab (see The Values tab), stops the clock: its time adds to no figure, and the moves into and out of it still count in Sojourn Status Change Count, so a Case that went New, Waiting on Customer, Working shows 2 when Waiting on Customer does not count. A closed status always counts, so the close figures do not change. The owner figures follow the object's owner tracking: under Users only no queue minutes are counted, and a move from one user through a queue to another is one handoff; under Queues only no agent minutes are counted.

docs.title: When they change
docs.text:
Sojourn recomputes the figures from the Case's Status and Owner Intervals whenever one of them opens or closes: on every save, and after a catch up, a backfill, or a repair. A Case that missed an update, for example because a save was close to a Salesforce limit, is corrected by its next change.

Every Case gets its figures whoever saves it: Sojourn writes them itself, so agents do not need edit access to these fields, and the fields stay read-only for everyone but Sojourn admins. A catch up, backfill, repair, or the nightly Reconcile writes the figures in its own run, so the Case's Last Modified Date moves to that run's time.

docs.title: Sojourn's own update of the Case
docs.text:
Sojourn writes the figures with one more update of the Case, in the same transaction, right after a save that opens a Status or Owner Interval and after a Case is created. That update carries only the eight Sojourn fields, but your own Case automation runs for it like for any update: validation rules, before-update triggers, and Flows or processes set to run every time a record is edited. Set automation that should run once per user save to run only when the fields it cares about change.

If automation that runs during Sojourn's update changes the Case's Status or Owner, Sojourn records that change as it happens, like any other save, and recomputes the figures, unless a validation rule refuses Sojourn's update of another Case in the same save; then the next change to the Case or the Reconcile job records it. A validation rule that refuses Sojourn's update leaves the user's save in place; the refused figures are an entry in the Error Log, and the next change to the Case recomputes them.

Automation on Sojourn's Interval object is different. If a Flow or trigger that runs when an Interval is saved changes a Tracked field of the Case, Lead, or Opportunity the Interval belongs to, in the same save, Sojourn does not record that change as it happens; the next Reconcile run records it. Keep automation on Intervals from writing to the record they belong to.

Often missed. The figures are fields on Case, so they show only where you add them. Add them to your Case page layouts and to Case reports; Sojourn does not change your layouts.

docs.title: Add them to a Case page
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Object Manager, then Case, then Page Layouts, and choose your layout.
  2. Drag the Sojourn fields into a section, for example one named Service metrics, and save.

You are done when

  • Closing a Case shows Sojourn First Closed At and its business minutes on the Case page.

docs.title: Build a dashboard
docs.text: Sojourn Dashboards is a tab where each manager builds their own dashboards of where the time went. A dashboard is yours alone: nobody else sees it, and you see only your own. It is part of the Plus plan; on the Free plan the tab shows what it offers and how to get Plus, and the Sojourn reports and dashboards stay on Free.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need the Sojourn Manager or Sojourn Admin permission set, which include the Sojourn Dashboards permission and the tab. See Assign permission sets.
  • The charts read Interval Summaries, which the nightly Summaries job builds. See Run the jobs. Open now and Longest open are counted live.

After an upgrade. The charts for everyone read summary rows that the Summaries job writes from the first night after the upgrade. To fill past months at once, open Sojourn Settings, then Summaries, and select Rebuild under Rebuild summaries. See Summaries.

docs.title: Start a dashboard
docs.text:
1. Open the Sojourn Dashboards tab in the Sojourn app.
  2. On an empty dashboard, select Start from Support desk for ten charts to begin with, or Edit layout to start from an empty grid.
  3. Choose the Tracked object and Tracked field above the charts. The filters apply to every chart on the dashboard and are kept with it.
  4. Choose the Period (7, 30, or 90 days), Business hours or Calendar hours, and an Owner, or Everyone.

The line at the right of the filters says when the summaries were last built and when Open now was counted.

To switch dashboards, select the dashboard's name. The list also has New dashboard. You can keep up to 20 dashboards with up to 20 charts each, or fewer when your admin sets lower limits (see Set what dashboards start with). A new dashboard opens on the Tracked field, period, and hours your admin chose; a saved one keeps its own filters.

docs.title: The charts
docs.text:
Chart What it shows Number One figure for the period: Open Intervals now, Intervals, Average hours, Breaches, or Goal met, with the period before Bars Each value against its Goal, or each owner against the team average Trend The busiest values in each day, week, or month: three unless your admin chose one or two Share Each value group's share of the period's time, or each value's when the field has no value groups Heatmap Breaches or Intervals for each value with each of the busiest owners (12 unless your admin chose), and Others Table The open Intervals furthest past their Goal (50 unless your admin chose), with each record's time against its Goal

The owner charts, Bars by owner and the Heatmap, show owners only: Intervals of records with no owner, such as a tracked child in a master-detail relationship, are left out of their bars, Others, and the team average, and the Owner list offers only owners. The charts for Everyone still count them.

Goal met is the share of the Intervals that had a Goal when the stay began that finished within it. Intervals in a value with no Goal are left out, so a value, owner, or period where none had a Goal shows a dash, not 100 percent. A Number of Goal met shows the dash alone then, with no On track or Down state.

After upgrading to this version. Summary rows built before it do not count which Intervals had a Goal, so Goal met shows a dash wherever a chart adds one up, even after the nightly Summaries job adds a late Interval to the row. Run Rebuild summaries once after the upgrade, over the months the charts reach back to. A month a purge has cut into cannot be rebuilt, so Goal met shows a dash for it.

A day, week, or month with no Intervals has no average. A Trend of average hours leaves a gap in the line there, a Number's sparkline leaves the bar out, and the chart's table and its tooltip show a dash, which a screen reader reads as "No Intervals"; counts and Breaches show 0.

Point at a bar, cell, or line to see its numbers. Select Expand on a chart to see it full screen; on a Trend, drag across the chart to zoom into a range. The chart's menu has Edit chart, Show as table, Duplicate, and Remove from dashboard.

A Trend draws a week or a month the dashboard's period covers only part of, such as the first and last week of a 30-day period, and says so: its axis label, its tooltip, and its row in the table read "part week" (or "part month"), and the legend adds a note when there is room. Those periods hold fewer days than the others, so read them as part of the trend, not as a drop or a rise.

You can set the zoom range without the mouse. In the full-screen view of a Trend, From and To list each period's start; choose one in each to zoom into that range. A range always holds at least two periods: if you choose a start at or after the other end, the other end moves with it. Choosing the whole range again means no zoom. Reset zoom returns the chart to the whole range and puts focus on From.

A chart adds up month totals instead of day totals, and its subtitle ends with "by month", in two cases. The first is when its period reaches back further than the roll-up days, since a complete purge run removes the day totals older than that (see Summaries); a Number counts the period before as well, so with the roll-up at 35 days a 30-day Number reads month totals, and with it at 400, the default, every chart reads day totals. The second is a lot of Intervals over a long period. The measures mean the same, but a 30-day period then starts at the beginning of its first month, so it counts a few more days, and a Number compares with the same number of whole months before, which its caption names. If even the month totals are more than one chart can add up, the chart says so in place of its numbers: choose a shorter period or one owner.

docs.title: Edit the layout
docs.text:
1. Select Edit layout.
  2. Drag a chart from Components onto the grid, or select one and press Enter to add it at the bottom.
  3. Drag a chart to move it. Charts snap to the dots, and the charts in the way move down.
  4. Drag a chart's right edge, bottom edge, or corner to resize it. Each chart type stops at its smallest and largest size, and the badge says why.
  5. Select a chart to change its title, type, measure, grouping, or size on the right. With the keyboard, the arrow keys on a chart's handle move it, and Shift with an arrow resizes it.
  6. Select Save layout, or Cancel to keep the dashboard as it was. Undo and Redo go back and forward up to 50 steps.
