To rename or delete the dashboard, select an empty part of the grid while editing: the right panel shows the dashboard's name and Delete dashboard.

Sojourn Dashboards writes each dashboard's layout and filters itself. If they are changed another way, for example by a data load or through the API, and gain a key Sojourn does not write or a value of the wrong type, the dashboard stays in the list, counted with no charts, but does not open: the page says why. It opens again once its layout and filters are saved again with only the keys Sojourn writes; or delete the dashboard's record.

docs.title: Print or save as PDF
docs.text:
1. Select Print or PDF.
  2. Choose Black and white or Colour, A4 or Letter, and whether to add the data tables at the end. The preview starts with what your admin chose, Black and white, A4, and the data tables unless they changed it.
  3. Select Print. For a PDF, choose Save as PDF in the print dialog, with landscape pages.

In black and white, each series has its own pattern, dash, and marker, so the charts read without colour. If a chart's numbers cannot be read when you print, its data table at the end says why in place of the table.

docs.title: Set what dashboards start with
docs.text:
A Sojourn Admin sets, for everyone who builds a dashboard, what a new dashboard opens on, what the charts show, what the print preview starts with, and the limits. Open Sojourn Settings, then Dashboards under Data. The settings are on the Plus plan: on the Free plan the screen shows them with their controls off and the Plus notice. Each setting names its default, and a blank box always means the default. Changing a setting needs the Customize Application permission, as the other Sojourn settings do.

Card Setting What it sets Default Range or choices New dashboards Tracked field The Tracked field a new dashboard opens on The first Tracked field Your Tracked fields New dashboards Period The days a new dashboard covers 30 days 7, 30, or 90 days New dashboards Hours Business or calendar hours for a new dashboard Business hours Business or Calendar hours Charts Owners in an owner chart The busiest owners Bars by owner and the Heatmap show; the rest add up as Others 12 5 to 20 Charts Owners in the Owner filter The busiest owners of the period the Owner filter lists 50 10 to 100 Charts Values in a Trend The busiest values a Trend draws, a line each 3 1 to 3 Charts Rows in Longest open The open Intervals furthest past their Goal the table lists 50 10 to 100 Printing Colours What the print preview starts in Black and white Black and white or Colour Printing Paper The paper the print preview starts with A4 A4 or Letter Printing Data tables Whether the preview adds each chart's numbers at the end Added On or off Advanced Dashboards for each person The most dashboards one person can have 20 1 to 20 Advanced Charts on a dashboard The most charts one dashboard can hold 20 4 to 20 Advanced Summary rows one chart adds up Past this, a chart reads month totals; still past it, the chart asks for a shorter period or one owner 20,000 5,000 to 40,000

Each card has its own save. A number outside its range is refused, for example "Owners in an owner chart: enter a whole number from 5 to 20, or leave it blank for the default, 12.", and nothing on that card is saved.

  • A saved dashboard keeps its own filters; only new dashboards open on the Tracked field, period, and hours here. If the Tracked field you chose is no longer tracked, new dashboards open on the first Tracked field again.
  • Anyone printing can still change the colours, paper, and data tables in the preview.
  • A lower limit never removes a dashboard or a chart. Someone over a lower limit keeps every dashboard and cannot add one; a dashboard over a lower chart limit keeps its charts, can still be saved, and cannot gain one.
  • A larger summary row limit lets a long period stay on day totals for longer, and each chart takes longer to load; a smaller one moves to month totals sooner.

These settings travel in the settings file, and Reset to defaults puts them back.

You are done when your dashboard shows its charts for the Tracked field you chose, and opens the same way the next time you open the tab.

docs.title: Use the Get started guide
docs.text:
Get started is the first line of the Sojourn Settings menu, under Capture. It lists the twelve steps that take a new install to a first report, in four phases. Each step shows its status as Sojourn found it in your org just now, why the step matters, what it changes, what to do, and a How it works behind the scenes note that stays folded until you open it. A button opens the screen or the Setup page where you do the step. Where a step needs reading before you do it, a link such as Which set for whom or Run the jobs on the guide opens the page on this site that covers it; it shows while the step is not done, and on step 1 always. While the guide is not complete, step 4 done offers Add another object, which opens Tracked objects with the Add object dialog open. Only people with the Sojourn Admin permission set see the guide; see Assign permission sets.

Sojourn checks your org and never does a step for you: it changes nothing in Setup, and assigning a permission set or making a Flow stays your work.

docs.title: When the guide opens
docs.text:
Sojourn Settings opens on Get started while Open this guide first when Sojourn Settings opens is on and a required step is left. The switch is on after install. You can turn it off or on at any time from the progress card at the top of the guide.

Sojourn turns the switch off by itself the first time it finds every required step done and no step needing attention. Sojourn Settings then opens on the Overview, and Get started stays in the menu. Turning the switch off is a settings change, so it needs the Customize Application permission, which system administrators have. Without it, the guide says that Open this guide first could not be turned off, and Sojourn tries again the next time an admin who holds that permission opens Sojourn Settings.

A link that names its own screen, such as the addresses in Install Sojourn, opens that screen and not the guide.

docs.title: What each status means
docs.text:
Status What it means Done Sojourn found the step true. The step folds to a line, with the date where a record holds its own date. To do A step that counts is not true yet. Not started An optional step with nothing done yet. It carries the Optional tag and never holds the guide open. Needs attention Step 5 only: a Tracked object needs a capture Flow and has none. The step names the object, and the guide is not complete while it stands. Could not check Sojourn could not read what the step needs. The step says what it could not read and does not block the others. A required step at Could not check is not done.

Every step that is not done opens by itself, and every done step folds to its line and its buttons. Choose a step's title to open or fold it.

A step stays true only while the org does. Sojourn reads every step again each time Sojourn Settings opens, so a job turned off, a Flow deactivated, or a sandbox refresh puts the step back to To do or Needs attention.

docs.title: Could not check
docs.text:
Most reads run as you, in user mode, so a step shows Could not check when your user is refused the data. The permissions that matter:

  • View Setup and Configuration is needed to read the capture Flows (steps 4 and 5) and the edition (step 1). Without it, step 1 is still decided on your business hours, and the edition is left out.
  • View Setup and Configuration, Assign Permission Sets, or Manage Users: any one of them lets Sojourn count who holds the permission sets (step 2).
  • Steps 3, 7, 11, and 12 run no read that can fail. Step 6 reads the scheduled jobs the way the Jobs screen does, so no user permission applies to it. Steps 8, 9, and 10 read Sojourn's own objects, which Sojourn Admin grants, so Could not check there means the read failed: choose Check again, and if it happens again, ask a Sojourn admin to look at the Health Monitor.

The exact reads, and what each needs, are in the security notes that ship with the package.

docs.title: Check again
docs.text: Check again in the progress card reads all twelve steps again and shows when it last did ("Checked just now", "Checked 5 minutes ago"). Steps 2, 5 (Re-check Flows), and 10 carry a button of their own beside their other buttons, since you fix those elsewhere and then come back. Each of them is the same single re-read of every step.

docs.title: The four phases and twelve steps
docs.text: The tables say what makes each step Done and link to the page that covers the step; this page does not repeat them. Steps marked Optional never hold the guide open.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Step Done when Read 1. Check the prerequisites Setup has at least one active business hours. The edition is shown and never blocks the step. Check the prerequisites 2. Assign permission sets At least one person holds Sojourn Admin, and at least one holds Sojourn Manager or Sojourn User, directly or through a permission set group. Assign permission sets

docs.title: Capture
docs.text: Step Done when Read 3. Turn on capture for the org Tracking enabled is on. A new org starts with it on, so this step begins Done. Track an object 4. Track your first object An active Tracked object has an active Tracked field, and its capture pill reads Tracked by package or Flow active. Track Cases and open your first report 5. Set up a capture Flow for other objects Every active Tracked object other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity has an active capture Flow. Required only when such an object exists, which is the Plus plan; an object whose pill reads Flow missing makes the step Needs attention. Track an object

docs.title: Keep Intervals current
docs.text: Step Done when Read 6. Turn on the jobs Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries are all scheduled. Run the jobs 7. Choose how long to keep Intervals On the Plus plan, a retention choice is saved; Keep everything counts as a choice. On the Free plan the step is Done by itself, because Sojourn keeps everything. Keep or purge Intervals

docs.title: Make the time useful
docs.text:
Step Done when Read 8. Set goals and queue business hours (Optional) At least one active Goal that you can see exists; a Goal you deactivated is not counted. The step also counts the queues with their own business hours. Set goals and business hours 9. Backfill past Intervals (Optional) A History Backfill has completed, or a Catch up has run, on any Tracked object. Backfill past Intervals 10. Check capture is live and open your first report You can see at least one Interval. Once it is Done, the step also says how many Intervals there are and which Sources wrote them. Track Cases and open your first report 11. Put the timeline on record pages (Optional) You mark it done; Sojourn cannot read your record pages. Show the timeline on a record 12. Decide who sees the packaged dashboards (Optional) You mark it done; Sojourn cannot read who the dashboards run as or who their folder is shared with. Install Sojourn

On the Free plan, the steps that belong to the Plus plan carry a Plus plan tag that links to Upgrade to Plus; see Free and Plus plans.

docs.title: The two steps you mark done
docs.text:
Steps 11 and 12 are changes in Setup and in Lightning App Builder, which Sojourn cannot read. Each shows a Mark as done box. Tick it once the work is finished, and the step shows who marked it and when ("Marked done by Alex Dawson on 22 Oct 2026"), and counts as Done from then on. To take a mark back, untick the box: the step returns to Not started, and the other step keeps its own mark. Saving or taking back a mark needs the Customize Application permission, like the other Settings saves. Sojourn keeps the marks as org settings.

The marks and the switch travel in the settings file: a set-up made in a sandbox and imported in production brings Open this guide first and both marks with it. A mark whose person is not in the other org shows the date without a name. See Move settings between orgs.

docs.title: The Overview banner and the menu count
docs.text:
While the guide is not complete, whether or not it opens first, the Overview opens with a banner above its header card: how many steps are done, the required steps still to go by name, and any object that needs attention, with Continue to open Get started. The banner takes the place of the Overview's retention line, since the guide covers retention, and leaves once every required step is done and none needs attention.

The Get started line in the menu shows a count such as 3 of 12 while any of the twelve steps is not done. It shows no count when all twelve are done, and no count and no banner when Sojourn could not load the guide.

You are done when

  • Every required step reads Done, or Done by itself on the Free plan, and no step needs attention.
  • The guide shows Set up complete, and Open this guide first is off.
  • Sojourn Settings opens on the Overview with no banner.

docs.title: Set goals and business hours
docs.text: A goal says how long a record should stay in a value. Business hours say which minutes count. Both are set in Sojourn Settings, under Time, beside Alerts, which decides who hears about a Breach.

docs.title: Set goals
docs.text:
Open Goals. Choose the Tracked object and the Tracked field; the field starts on the object's status field. Each value of the field has a row, with Any value first:

  • Target, business minutes: how long an Interval in this value should last. Leave it blank for no goal.
  • Warn at, percent: the share of the goal, from 1 to 100, at which an Interval is flagged as a warning. Leave it blank for no warning. A Goal saved any other way, from a data load or the API, is refused outside 1 to 100 too.

On the status field, a closed value is marked closed and takes no goal. The closed values are the ones capture uses: the object's Closed values, or, for Case with none listed and Status as its status field, the statuses Case marks closed.

A value's own goal wins over Any value. Choose Save goals. New Intervals carry the goal; Intervals already open keep the one they started with. An Interval that runs past its goal is a Breach: the Live values job flags one that is still open, and a stay is flagged when it closes past its goal.

A warning is flagged the same way, earlier. When an Interval's business minutes reach the warn percent of its goal, Sojourn ticks Warning on the Interval and sets Warned At to the moment it got there: the time it entered the value plus that share of the goal, in its business hours. The Live values job flags an open Interval; a stay is flagged when it closes. A breached Interval is always a warning too. Once set, a flag keeps its time. A new Interval carries its warn threshold as Warn Minutes, beside Goal Minutes: the warn percent of the goal when the Interval started. Changing the goal or turning it off later changes neither the warning nor the Breach of an Interval already started. Reports on Intervals can filter on Warning, and the timeline names a warning in a stay's goal, as it names a breach.

The Breach alerts card has its own screen, Alerts, under Time. It is for every Tracked object: its switch, Also email when a stay closes past its goal, decides whether the breach alert email also goes for stays that closed late, or only while an Interval is still open (the default). See Email a breach alert.

Clearing a target turns the goal off. Goals are never deleted, so Intervals that point at one keep it.

docs.title: Split goals by a second field
docs.text:
A value can have a different goal for each value of one more field on the record: a Case in New might get 30 minutes at High priority and 4 hours at Low. The card Split goals by, below the goals, sets this for the Tracked field chosen above.

Under A goal for each value of, choose the field to split by, or None for no split. The list holds the object's picklist and checkbox fields you can read, other than the Tracked field itself; a checkbox splits into Checked and Not checked. Once the split is saved, the card shows a matrix:

  • A row for each value of the Tracked field, with Any value first. Closed values have no row, since they have no goal. Values that do not count are not offered, and a Tracked field that keeps only the change takes no goals.
  • A column for each value of the split field, then the Any column (for example Any priority). The Any column is the value's own goal, the same target as the Target, business minutes box above; changing one changes the other.
  • Each cell is a target in business minutes. Leave a cell blank for no goal. A cell has no Warn at of its own: it takes the Warn at of its value's row.

When an Interval starts, Sojourn reads the record's value of the split field and takes the most specific goal that is set, in this order:

  1. The value, with the record's split value (a cell).
  2. The value, with any split value (the Any column).
  3. Any value, with the record's split value.
  4. Any value, with any split value.

So a blank cell uses the Any column, and a record whose split field is blank takes the value's own goal. Choose Save goals to save the goals and the matrix together. As with every goal, the Interval keeps the goal it started with.

To split by a different field, choose it and then Save goals. The screen warns you first: the goals split by the old field turn off when you save. They are kept, not deleted, but no longer apply, and Intervals already started keep their goals. After the save, the matrix shows the new field's values, empty, ready for targets. Choosing None and saving turns the split off the same way, and the value goals above go on applying.

docs.title: Give record types their business hours
docs.text: Open the object under Tracked objects and choose the Records tab. Business hours by record type lists each record type of the object; choose business hours for one, or leave it on Use the next rule, then choose Save. A record of that type uses those hours ahead of the queue's and the object's, so a Support record type can keep support hours whichever queue holds the record. An object with no record types shows no rows; set its hours under Business hours in Object settings on the same tab.

docs.title: Give queues their business hours
docs.text:
Open Business hours. The card at the top names the org default, the hours used when nothing more specific applies; change it on the Overview. The Queues table lists every queue with the objects it takes. Choose business hours for a queue, or leave it on Use the next rule, then choose Save.

For each Interval, Sojourn uses the first of these that is set. The card Which business hours an Interval uses, below the Queues table, lists the same order:

  1. The Tracked field's own business hours.
  2. A business hours field on the record, when the Tracked object names one.
  3. The record type's business hours, set on the object's Records tab.
  4. The queue's business hours, while a queue owns the record.
  5. The Tracked object's business hours.
  6. The Sojourn default on the Overview, then the org's default business hours.

Business hours Salesforce cannot use (deleted or inactive) fall back to calendar time, and Sojourn logs that once.

Changes apply to Intervals that start after you save.

You are done when

  • An Interval created after you save shows the goal on its record.
  • With split goals, an Interval for a record with a split value that has a cell carries that cell's target as its goal.
  • An Interval for a record of a record type with its own hours counts business minutes in those hours.
  • An Interval for a record owned by a mapped queue counts business minutes in that queue's hours.

docs.title: Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor
docs.text: The Health Monitor tab in the Sojourn app shows whether field tracking is working right now. It is separate from Sojourn Settings, so a support or operations group can watch Sojourn and fix its errors without changing its configuration.

docs.title: Who can open it
docs.text: Give people the Sojourn Health Monitor permission set; the Sojourn Admin permission set includes it. Without either, the tab says which permission set is needed and loads nothing. Health Monitor users can create the missing Interval, ignore, or resolve any error. Fixes that change configuration open Sojourn Settings, so for Health Monitor users without Sojourn Admin the page says "Ask a Sojourn admin" instead.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• The banner reads Healthy, Needs attention, or Not working, with one line that says what needs you. Check again reads everything afresh. How many open errors make it Needs attention or Not working is set on the Health screen; see Health thresholds.
  • Capture lists what stops Intervals being recorded: tracking off for the whole org, a Tracked object whose capture Flow is missing or cannot be read, a paused object or one waiting for Catch up, a failed backfill. On the Free plan, an object other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity shows "Plus plan needed" as information: it keeps its Intervals, and new changes are not recorded. If you cannot see Flows (you lack View Setup and Configuration and are not a Sojourn admin), an object captured by a Flow shows "Flow status hidden from you" as information: it does not change the overall status, and a Sojourn admin sees the real Flow status.
  • Jobs shows whether Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries are scheduled, their last run, and the next one. A job that is off shows as a warning until a Sojourn admin schedules it on the Jobs screen in Sojourn Settings; on a new install, that includes Summaries. A job scheduled by a user who is no longer active shows as a failure; turning it off and on again on the Jobs screen, as an active Sojourn admin, fixes it. Live values with an entry missing (for example after someone deleted one in Setup) shows as a warning with the minutes it still runs at; choosing the interval again on the Jobs screen restores it. A last run in which chunks failed shows as a failure that says how many, here and on the job's card on the Jobs screen; Salesforce's reason is in Setup, under Apex Jobs. A scheduled job that has not run for longer than its schedule allows, plus the late hours set on the Health screen (2 by default), shows as a warning that says when it last ran: Live values counts its minutes between runs, and Reconcile and Summaries a day. A job you have just turned on again counts from then, not from its last run before. For a Sojourn admin, each of these carries its fix, Schedule it in Settings for a job that is off and Check the job in Settings for the others, and both open the Jobs screen.
  • Errors counts the errors that need you, those in the last 24 hours, and those fixed in the last 24 hours, by type.
  • Recent errors lists the latest, each with its fix.

docs.title: Health thresholds
docs.text:
A Sojourn admin sets what the banner counts on the Health screen: open Sojourn Settings, then Health under Operations. The Health Monitor applies the thresholds for everyone who opens it. Saving them needs the Customize Application permission, as the other org-wide settings do.

Setting What it does Default Range Needs attention when open errors are more than The banner reads Needs attention when more errors than this need you. 0 0 to 10,000 Something is wrong when open errors are more than The banner reads Not working when more errors than this need you, and says how many against the number you set. Blank, never 1 to 10,000, or blank A job is late after, hours A scheduled job that has not run for this many hours past its schedule is a warning under Jobs. 2 1 to 72

With the defaults the banner works as it always has: any open error needs attention, and open errors alone never make it Not working; only the failures under Capture and Jobs do. Errors within the first number still show in the Errors counts and the list; they only stop turning the banner amber.

Each box shows the saved number, or the default while none is saved. Clear a box to go back to its default (for the second one, never), then choose Save thresholds. A notice says "Health thresholds are saved." A number outside its range is refused with the range, for example "A job is late after (hours): enter a whole number from 1 to 72, or leave it blank for the default, 2.", and nothing is saved. Reset to defaults on the Advanced screen clears all three; see Tune the advanced settings. The Health screen is on the Free and the Plus plan.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The Errors tab lists Error Log rows by status, type, object, and age. Select rows to Create intervals, Mark resolved, or Ignore them together. The list shows the newest 200 errors that match the filters; when more match, it says "Showing the newest 200 errors" and Select all takes only those 200. Resolve or ignore them, or narrow the filters, to reach older ones. Open a row to see what happened, why, how to fix it, and the technical details for support. When a job such as Backfill or Purge fails for a reason Sojourn did not describe itself, the message says so in a fixed sentence, and Salesforce's own words are in the technical details, which only Sojourn admins see: Sojourn Health Monitor has no access to the Error Log's Stack field, on this tab, on the record page, or in reports.

Type What happened How to fix it Limit The save that changed the record was already close to a Salesforce governor limit, so Sojourn stepped aside to protect it. Choose Create interval, or leave it: the nightly reconcile retries Limit and DML errors older than an hour, up to three times. If many come from one import, pause the object before the next import and catch up after it. DML Salesforce refused to save the Interval, often because of a validation rule, a required field, or another app's trigger. Fix the cause the technical details name, then choose Create interval, or let reconcile retry it. Config A Tracked field names a field that was deleted or renamed, or that Sojourn can no longer read; or automation on an object changed a tracked field on every save, and Sojourn stopped following the saves three levels deep. In Sojourn Settings, remove the field or choose its replacement, then mark the error resolved. For the save loop, find the Flow or trigger on the named object that changes the field each time it saves, and stop it repeating. Business hours No usable business hours applied, so calendar minutes were recorded as business minutes. Choose default business hours in Sojourn Settings, or hours on the Tracked object, then mark the error resolved. Unknown Sojourn hit an error it did not expect. The user's save still went through. Choose Create interval. If it happens again, send the technical details to CloudAlgo support.

Create interval records the change at the time it happened and marks the error Resolved. It is refused when later changes to the same field were already recorded, because the change can no longer be placed; ignore the error, or run a History backfill to rebuild the record's history. It is also refused, with the reason, when the change left blank a field that starts timing at its first value, or when the value is already recorded: there is no Interval to create, so ignore the error. The nightly reconcile counts each refusal as a retry and adds its reason to the error's message, so such an error stops being retried after three tries instead of looping.

The same Create Interval action is on every Error Log record page.

You are done when

  • The banner reads Healthy, or every item it lists has a fix under way.
  • The Health screen shows the thresholds your team agreed, or the defaults.
  • No error in the Errors tab reads Needs you without a reason you know.

docs.title: Before you install
docs.text: Check the edition, features, and permissions in Check the prerequisites. Sojourn installs on the Free plan; see Free and Plus plans.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Release 1 is in development, so there is no AppExchange listing yet. Early access customers receive a package version ID from CloudAlgo. Request a package version ID.

  1. Install the package version, using the ID you were given:

    sf package install --package 04t... --target-org my-sandbox --wait 20

  2. Assign permission sets, as described in Assign permission sets.

  3. Decide who sees the dashboards. The four Sojourn dashboards run as the admin who installed Sojourn, and their folder is open to everyone, so every viewer sees what that admin sees, including the Case numbers, subjects, and owners that SLA Health and Desk Productivity list. Do one of these:
    • In Setup, open Dashboards, edit each Sojourn dashboard, and under View dashboard as choose a user whose access fits your viewers, or The dashboard viewer if your edition allows dynamic dashboards.
    • Or share the Sojourn Dashboards folder only with the people who may see that admin's data.
  4. Open the Sojourn app from the App Launcher.

You are done when

  • The Sojourn app appears in the App Launcher.
  • Each Sojourn dashboard runs as a user you chose, or its folder is shared only with the people who may see the installing admin's data.
  • The app opens with an Intervals tab in its navigation, with three list views: All Intervals, Open Intervals, and Breached Intervals. An Interval record shows its value, time, goal, Live values, and the record's snapshot in sections; its fields are read only, because Sojourn writes them.

docs.title: After you install: the Get started guide
docs.text: The first time an admin opens Sojourn Settings, it opens on Get started: twelve steps in four phases, each showing what Sojourn found in your org just now, with a button to the screen where you do the step. It covers the permission sets, the jobs, your first Tracked object, retention, and the rest of the list on this page, and Sojourn stops opening it first once every required step is done. See Use the Get started guide.

docs.title: Three things to do first
docs.text:
• Give yourself Sojourn Admin, and check Customize Application. Sojourn Settings needs the Sojourn Admin permission set, and saving the org-wide settings (on the Overview, and the Alerts, Jobs, Health, Summaries, Retention and purge, and Advanced screens) also needs the Customize Application permission, which system administrators have. Without it, the screen says why it cannot save. See Assign permission sets.
  • Turn on the jobs. Installing Sojourn schedules nothing, so Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries are Off until you choose Turn on for each on the Jobs screen, and the Health Monitor shows them as warnings until then. See Run the jobs.
  • Open the Sojourn app. Installing does not make Sojourn your default app. Find Sojourn in the App Launcher; its tabs are Sojourn Settings, Health Monitor, Sojourn Dashboards, and Intervals.

docs.title: Omni-Channel
docs.text: To record agent work from Omni-Channel, install the Sojourn Omni-Channel package after this one. It needs Omni-Channel turned on; this package does not. See Track agent work in Omni-Channel.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Install the new package version over the installed one, with the same command and the new ID. Intervals, settings, and scheduled jobs stay, and a later version never changes the packaged reports and dashboards you already have. Read the changelog first.

docs.title: After you upgrade
docs.text:
From the first published version on, each package version gets its own entry in the changelog, named by its version number, and the entry ends with an After you upgrade list: anything to do once the new version is in, such as a job to turn on, a permission set to assign, a summary rebuild, or a report to add by hand, because a later version never replaces the reports and dashboards you have. A version that needs nothing says so.

Version 1.0.0, when it is published, is the first version, so there is nothing to upgrade from: install it new and follow the steps on this page. Salesforce never upgrades a beta package version, so if a sandbox holds a Sojourn beta, uninstall it first, as Uninstall Sojourn describes.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: See Uninstall Sojourn: turn off the jobs first, and keep a copy of anything you need.

docs.title: Move settings from a sandbox
docs.text: Set Sojourn up once in a sandbox, then export the settings as a file and import them in production. See Move settings between orgs.

docs.title: Links into Sojourn
docs.text:
Each Sojourn Settings screen and Health Monitor tab has its own address, so a link can open it directly. The address follows you as you move, so you can copy it from the browser at any time. Add these to your org's address, after /lightning/n/. Each tab's name starts with the package's namespace, sojourn__, as in every installed org:

Opens Address The Overview, or its Capture for the whole org card sojourn__Settings?c__screen=overview (add &c__section=capture) Tracked objects sojourn__Settings?c__screen=objects Tracked objects, with the Add object dialog open sojourn__Settings?c__screen=objects&c__section=add A Tracked object, by API name, on its Fields tab sojourn__Settings?c__screen=objects&c__object=Case ...on one of its tabs: fields, records, backfill, live-values, or advanced sojourn__Settings?c__screen=objects&c__object=Case&c__section=backfill ...on its Records tab, at Closed when sojourn__Settings?c__screen=objects&c__object=Case&c__section=closed-when Business hours, Goals, Alerts, Jobs, Health, Export settings, or Advanced sojourn__Settings?c__screen=hours (or goals, alerts, jobs, health, export, advanced) Goals of one object sojourn__Settings?c__screen=goals&c__object=Lead Retention and purge, at Keep Intervals or Purge runs sojourn__Settings?c__screen=retention (add &c__section=keep or purge) Summaries, at Roll-up or Rebuild summaries sojourn__Settings?c__screen=summaries&c__section=rollup (or rebuild) The Health Monitor's errors, by status sojourn__Health_Monitor?c__tab=errors&c__status=New (or Resolved, Ignored, All)

A link to an object by its record Id, c__trackedObjectId, as the Health Monitor's fixes use, works too.

Get started's Add another object uses the Add object link. When you close the dialog, Tracked objects stays open and &c__section=add leaves the address, so a reload does not open the dialog again.

Links saved before the Jobs, Alerts, and Summaries screens and the object's tabs open the same card in its new place, and the address changes to the new link, so copy it again:

  • c__screen=overview&c__section=jobs opens Jobs.
  • c__screen=goals&c__section=alerts, with or without c__object, opens Alerts.
  • c__screen=retention&c__section=rebuild opens Summaries at Rebuild summaries.
  • On an object, c__section=settings opens the Records tab, and closed-when the Records tab at Closed when; fields, backfill, and live-values open those tabs.

A link to an object that is not tracked yet opens Tracked objects and says so.

docs.title: Run the jobs
docs.text: Every Sojourn job runs as the admin who schedules or starts it, with that admin's access, and the Health Monitor shows each run. No job calls a service outside Salesforce. Schedule the jobs as a dedicated, long-lived Sojourn admin user rather than a person who may leave: if that user is deactivated, every run fails, and the Health Monitor says so and names the user.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text:
Open Sojourn Settings, then Jobs under Operations. Each job has its own card with an On or Off pill, its last run, and its next one: Turn on schedules a job, Change saves a new interval or time, and Turn off stops it. A run that is still going when the next one is due is skipped. The Overview keeps one line saying how the jobs stand, for example "Live values On, every 15 minutes. Reconcile Off. Summaries On, daily at 01:00.", with Open Jobs.

Job When What it does Plan Live values Every 10, 15, 20, 30, or 60 minutes Keeps minutes to date and breach flags current on open Intervals. On Plus, also writes the minute fields on records of objects with Write live values to the record on Free and Plus; the minute fields are Plus Reconcile Daily, at the time you choose Closes and flags every Interval of records that were deleted or merged, tracks records brought back from the Recycle Bin again, records values that changed without capture, and retries Limit and DML errors Free and Plus Summaries Daily, at the time you choose Counts closed Intervals into daily and monthly summary rows for reports. After it, purge runs when retention keeps a number of days Free and Plus; purge is Plus

Reconcile flags the closed Intervals of a deleted or merged record too, not only the open ones it closes. It reads them 2,000 at a time, one batch after another, for as long as the run has room, so one run flags them all for almost any record. A record with more than one run has room for is finished at the end of that run, when Reconcile looks again at the records it flagged, or by the next days' runs while the record is in the Recycle Bin.

When a record comes back from the Recycle Bin after Reconcile flagged it, its Intervals lose the flag and each Interval Reconcile closed at the deletion opens again, so the days in the Recycle Bin count in that value. Reconcile checks Closed at Deletion on the Intervals it closes, and only those open again: an Interval that had already ended stays ended, such as the owner stay of a record that was closed when it was deleted, or agent work that had finished. Summary rows only ever add, so for the 15 days a deleted record can be brought back, and one day more so the next Reconcile can open them again, Summaries and Rebuild summaries leave out the Intervals Reconcile closed at its deletion: once the 16 days have passed, each is counted as it closed, and if the record comes back, each is counted once, when it closes again. No stay is counted twice. Cases, Leads, and Opportunities are tracked again the moment they are undeleted; other objects at the next Reconcile, however many deleted records are still in the Recycle Bin, and a change made to such a record before then starts its Intervals again from that change.

Reconcile corrects Intervals that are open: a value that changed without capture closes the open Interval and opens the new value's. It never starts a field's first Interval, so a field with none, for example after a Fresh start, waits for its next change, and a blank field timed from its first value gets nothing until it has one.

docs.title: How far back Live values reaches
docs.text:
Live values refreshes open Intervals that started in the last 90 days, unless you change it. An Interval open longer than that keeps the minutes to date and breach flag of its last refresh, and so do the minute fields on its record: for a Case that has stayed in one status for four months, the Status Interval shows the minutes it had at 90 days, and a Goal it passes after that is flagged as a Breach only when the Interval closes.

To change the window, set Keep current for on the Live values card, from 1 to 365 days. The box shows the saved number, or 90 while none is saved, and its hint names the default; clear the box to go back to 90. The window saves with the card's Change, or Turn on when the job is off, before the schedule: a number outside 1 to 365 is refused with what to enter, and the schedule stays as it was. Turn off and Run now do not save it.

docs.title: Run a job now
docs.text:
Run now on a job's card starts one run of Live values, Reconcile, or Summaries straight away, as you, whether the job is scheduled or not. Its schedule stays as it is, and the run follows the same plan rules as a scheduled one: on the Free plan, a Live values run flags breaches and writes no minute fields. A notice says the run started, for example "Reconcile started.", and the Health Monitor shows the run. Run now is refused, with the reason, when:

  • that job is already running: "Live values is already running."
  • Salesforce already holds 100 batch jobs waiting to run, the most it allows: see When Salesforce already holds 100 batch jobs.

docs.title: Jobs you start
docs.text:
Job Started from Plan Catch up Catch up on the Tracked objects list, after a pause Free and Plus Backfill The Backfill tab of an object's screen; see Backfill past Intervals History and Seed are Plus; Fresh starts no job Purge now Purge now on Retention and purge; see Keep or purge Intervals Plus Rebuild summaries Rebuild on Summaries; see Summaries Free and Plus

One catch up and one purge run at a time across the org, and one backfill per object. A catch up and a backfill never run together: each is refused while the other runs. Catch up, Purge now, and Rebuild summaries run as batch jobs; Backfill runs as a chain of short jobs, one after another (see How a run works).

docs.title: When Salesforce already holds 100 batch jobs
docs.text:
Salesforce holds at most 100 batch jobs waiting to run, in the Apex flex queue, for the whole org: your own jobs and other apps' count too. Sojourn counts them before it starts any job, its scheduled runs and the jobs you start alike, and when 100 are waiting:

  • A job you start from a screen (Run now, Catch up, Run backfill, Purge now, or Rebuild) is refused, and nothing starts or changes. The notice names the job, for example "Salesforce is already holding 100 batch jobs, the most it allows, so Reconcile cannot start now. Try again once some have run; Apex Flex Queue in Setup lists them."
  • A scheduled run of Live values, Reconcile, or Summaries, and the purge that runs after Summaries, steps aside: it writes one row to the Error Log, for example "Reconcile did not start: Salesforce is already holding 100 batch jobs, the most it allows. The next run tries again.", and the next run tries again. The Health Monitor's Errors tab lists the row. While that row is open, later runs of the same job that step aside add no row, so a queue that stays full all day leaves one row per job, not one per run; once you resolve the row, the next run that steps aside writes a new one.

Apex Flex Queue in Setup lists the jobs that are waiting. Once some have run, Sojourn's jobs start again as usual.

Sojourn counts the queue and then starts the job, so two admins who start jobs at the same moment while 99 are waiting can both see room. The second start then fails with Salesforce's own message about the flex queue instead of Sojourn's; nothing is half-written, and you can start it again once some jobs have run.

docs.title: After a sandbox refresh
docs.text:
Salesforce does not copy scheduled Apex jobs when it creates or refreshes a sandbox, so in the new sandbox Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries are Off on the Jobs screen, and the Health Monitor shows each as a warning. Turn on the ones you want there, as a Sojourn admin of the sandbox. A job you turn on works on the sandbox's records only: Live values writes the minute fields on the sandbox's records, and a purge deletes the sandbox's Intervals, never production's.

A new or refreshed sandbox also sends only system email until you change its email deliverability in Setup, so the breach alert email does not go out from it until then.

Still to check in your sandbox, because it depends on the sandbox and on what it copied:

  • The plan. On the Free plan, Sojourn Settings shows the Plus notices. If the sandbox shows them and production is on the Plus plan, tell us.
  • The data. Which Intervals, summary rows, and purge files the sandbox holds follows its type and what it copies from production. The Usage card on the Overview counts what is there.

docs.title: Before you uninstall
docs.text: Turn off every scheduled job first, on the Jobs screen. See Uninstall Sojourn.

docs.title: Move settings between orgs
docs.text: Set Sojourn up once in a sandbox, then move the settings to production, or to another sandbox, as a file.

docs.title: What the file carries
docs.text:
• Tracking enabled and the default business hours.
  • The Live values window, the three limits Sojourn leaves for your own automation (queries, rows, and CPU), and the days before Day rows become Month rows.
  • The Omni-Channel statuses that start agent work.
  • The three Health thresholds: open errors for amber, open errors for red, and the hours after which a job is late.
  • The Dashboards settings: the Tracked field, period, and hours a new dashboard opens on, the owners, Trend values, and Longest open rows the charts show, what the print preview starts with, and the dashboard, chart, and summary row limits. The Tracked field may be one the file itself tracks.
  • Each Tracked object with its settings, including:
    • the lookup to fill on each Interval and the History backfill records per chunk;
    • which owners get an Interval, and whether a move between members of one queue keeps the owner's stay;
    • the records to track;
    • business hours by record type.
  • Each Tracked field, with the values that do not count, its value groups, its value colours, what an Interval keeps, and the field its goals are split by.
  • Each goal, with the split value it is for.
  • Queue business hours.
  • Get started: whether Sojourn Settings opens on the guide first, and the two steps marked done by hand, each with who marked it and when. A mark whose user is not in the org you import into keeps its date; the step then reads "Marked done on" the date, without a name.

Each setting is written as it applies in your org, so one you never changed is written as its default. The red Health threshold has no default: when it is blank the file says never, and an import of never leaves red blank in the other org. Retention, the archive, the purge part size, and each object's own retention are not in the file: production keeps what you chose there.

Business hours are written by name, and queues and record types by developer name, because record Ids differ between orgs.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: In the org you are copying from, open Sojourn Settings, then Data, then Export settings, and choose Export. Sojourn saves the file, named like sojourn-settings-2026-10-12.json, to your Files and opens it. Download it from the preview.

docs.title: Check the import
docs.text:
In the org you are copying to, open the same screen and choose Choose file. Sojourn reads the file and lists What the import will do: each Tracked object, Tracked field, goal, queue, and setting it will create, update, turn off, or skip, and why. Nothing has been changed yet.

  • An object or field this org does not have stops the whole import, and nothing is written. So does a field that records to track or a split goal names and this org does not have. Add the field, or remove it from the source org, and export again. A Name field or Snapshot field you cannot read in this org stops the import too, with "You cannot read" and the field's name, because Sojourn copies those values to everyone who reads Intervals; give yourself read access to the field, or choose another in the source org, and export again.
  • A queue or business hours this org does not have is skipped, with the reason; the rest still imports. Business hours by record type is skipped whole when one of its business hours or record types is missing.
  • A setting the screens would refuse is skipped with the reason the screen gives, and the rest still imports. For example:
    • a number outside its range, or a red threshold that is not a whole number or never;
    • an Omni-Channel status this org does not have, or a lookup that does not point to the object;
    • on the Free plan, a changed History chunk, changed Omni-Channel statuses, or a changed Dashboards setting;
    • a new dashboard's Tracked field that is not one of the Tracked fields, in this org or in the file;
    • an owner choice the Values tab does not offer, or a condition the Records tab would refuse;
    • a value that does not count that is closed, or that the field does not have;
    • a value in two groups, or a colour other than Tide, Harbor, Slate, or Mist;
    • keeping only the change on the status field or the field Closed when reads, or on a field with goals;
    • a split field that is not a picklist or checkbox.
  • A skipped setting stays as it was in this org. Sojourn never writes part of a setting.
  • A goal the Goals screen would refuse is skipped with its reason: a goal on a value that does not count, a goal on a field that keeps only the change, or a split value the split field does not have.
  • When the file changes the field a Tracked field's goals are split by, goals for the old split values that are not in the file are turned off, as on the Goals screen.
  • A Tracked object whose new status field, or Closed when field, keeps only the change is skipped with the reason.
  • A file from before these settings were carried leaves them as they are.
  • A file that is not a Sojourn settings file, or is from a later format, is refused.

docs.title: Apply
docs.text:
Choose Apply. Everything in the list is written together, or nothing is.

Turn on Replace what is here before checking to make this org match the file: Tracked fields and goals that are not in the file are turned off. Nothing is deleted, and Tracked objects that are not in the file are left as they are.

You are done when

  • Choosing the same file again lists nothing to change.

docs.title: Track agent work in Omni-Channel
docs.text: Omni-Channel assigns work to agents without a normal save of the record, so a Case trigger never sees the assignment. The Sojourn Omni-Channel package reads Omni-Channel's own agent work and records one Interval per assignment: when the work is assigned or opened, and when it ends.

docs.title: Before you install
docs.text:
• The org is on the Plus plan. On the Free plan the package installs, but no agent work is recorded; see Free and Plus plans.

  • Omni-Channel is turned on in the org. The package reads Omni-Channel's agent work, which exists only when Omni-Channel is on; the core Sojourn package does not need it.

  • The core Sojourn package is installed, and the object the work belongs to, for example Case, is a Tracked object.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Install the Sojourn Omni-Channel package version after the core package, with the ID you were given. It adds no tab, permission set, or setting screen.

docs.title: What it records
docs.text:
For each piece of work, Sojourn opens an Agent work Interval on the record with the agent as its value and its owner, and closes it with the business minutes when the work is closed, declined, canceled, transferred, or the agent becomes unavailable. One agent work Interval is open on a record at a time: a transfer closes the first agent's Interval and the next assignment opens a new one.

Agent work Intervals sit beside the record's other Intervals, with Tracked field set to Agent work and Source set to Omni-Channel. They take no Live values or goals, and do not count toward the 10 Tracked fields. Work on an object that is not tracked, or is paused, is not recorded, and a catch up does not replay it.

docs.title: Choose which statuses start the work
docs.text:
By default an Interval opens when the work is Assigned or Opened. To change it, open Sojourn Settings, then Advanced under Operations. On the Omni-Channel card, which shows when Omni-Channel is on, Agent work starts at lists the statuses: remove Assigned to start only when the agent opens the work, or add another status from the org's list, then choose Save statuses. At least one status stays chosen. The card shows whenever Omni-Channel is on, with or without the Sojourn Omni-Channel package; until the package is installed, the statuses are kept and nothing reads them. Reset to defaults on the same screen puts back Assigned and Opened; see Tune the advanced settings.

You are done when

  • After an agent accepts and closes a routed Case, the Case's Intervals show one Agent work Interval with that agent and its business minutes.

docs.title: Assign permission sets
docs.text:
Sojourn ships five permission sets. Give each person the one that matches what they do.

Permission set Give it to What it allows Sojourn Admin Admins who configure tracking Create, edit, and delete all Sojourn records, including Tracked objects, Tracked fields, Goals, and queue business hours. Includes the Sojourn Admin custom permission, and builds their own Sojourn Dashboards on the Plus plan. Saving the org-wide settings also needs Customize Application, which system administrators have. Sojourn Health Monitor A support or operations group Open the Health Monitor tab and act on errors: create the missing Interval, ignore, or resolve. Create, edit, and delete Intervals and Error Logs, with view and modify all, because repair closes other users' Intervals, but not the Error Log's Stack field, the technical details only Sojourn Admin reads; read the configuration. No access to Sojourn Settings. A trusted role: assign it only to the people who maintain Sojourn's data. A repair it runs leaves the Case figures it cannot edit unchanged. Sojourn Manager People who report on intervals Read all intervals and interval summaries, and read Goals and tracking configuration. On the Plus plan, build their own Sojourn Dashboards, which only they see. Sojourn User Everyone who should see intervals Read intervals, Goals, and Tracked objects, and the record timeline. Sojourn Site User Experience Cloud site users The record timeline on records they can open, and nothing else. It has no user license, so site users can hold it.

docs.title: Who sees which Intervals
docs.text:
Intervals are Public Read Only: anyone with a Sojourn permission set reads every Interval in reports and list views, including Intervals of records they cannot open. The record timeline shows a record's Intervals only to people who can open the record. Intervals hold only the values of the fields you chose to track, and the Sojourn User permission set has no access to the copied Opportunity amount or the snapshot fields.

To limit who reads Intervals, open Setup, then Sharing Settings, and set Interval to Private. Each person then sees the Intervals they own, which are the ones their own changes created, and those your sharing rules give them. Sojourn Manager and Sojourn Health Monitor include View All on Intervals, so people with them keep seeing every Interval. This setting governs reports and list views only: the record timeline follows the record's own sharing, so anyone who can open a record and has the Sojourn Timeline permission sees its full history there.

All five include the Sojourn Timeline permission, which the record timeline needs. The objects and rights each one grants are listed in Reference: Permission sets.

docs.title: Assign in Setup
docs.text:
1. In Setup, open Permission Sets.
  2. Select the permission set, then Manage Assignments, then Add Assignment.
  3. Choose the users and select Assign.

docs.title: Assign with the Salesforce CLI
docs.text:
sf org assign permset --name Admin --target-org my-sandbox

Often missed. Reports join intervals to Cases, Leads, and Opportunities. A manager also needs read access to those records to see them in a joined report.

You are done when

  • Each person has the Sojourn permission set for what they do; a Health Monitor user may also have Manager or User.
  • An admin sees the Sojourn Settings and Health Monitor tabs; a Health Monitor user sees the Health Monitor; a manager sees Intervals and Interval Summaries.

docs.title: Free and Plus plans
docs.text: Sojourn installs on the Free plan. The Plus plan adds tracking for any object, live minutes on the record, Backfill, the archive and purge, Omni-Channel agent work, and Sojourn Dashboards. We switch an org to Plus from our License Management Org: nothing is reinstalled and no setting changes, and the switch reaches your org within a few minutes. To move an org to Plus, choose Upgrade to Plus on any Plus notice in Sojourn Settings, which opens CloudAlgo billing.

docs.title: What each plan includes
docs.text:
Capability Free Plus Tracking Case, Lead, and Opportunity, with their status, owner, and other fields Yes Yes Tracking any other object, custom or standard, through the capture Flow template No Yes Goals, breach flags, and business hours Yes Yes The record timeline, the 19 reports and 4 dashboards in Sojourn Yes Yes Pause, Catch up, and the nightly Reconcile and Summaries jobs Yes Yes Live values: minutes in the current status and with the current owner, written on the record No Yes Backfill with History or Seed No Yes Purge after a number of days, and the archive No Yes Omni-Channel agent work and the Agent Handle Time report, with the Sojourn Omni-Channel package No Yes The Health Monitor, and settings export and import Yes Yes Sojourn Dashboards: your own dashboards, layout editor, zoom, and black and white print No Yes

On the Free plan, the Live values job still runs: it keeps minutes to date and breach flags current on open Intervals of Case, Lead, and Opportunity. Backfill offers Fresh, which starts each record with its next change.

docs.title: In Sojourn Settings
docs.text: Plus features stay visible on the Free plan, with their controls off and a note that they are in the Plus plan, with an Upgrade to Plus link. So do the settings that belong to them: the purge part size under Retention and purge, the History backfill chunk on an object's Advanced tab, and the Omni-Channel statuses on the Advanced screen. The Add object dialog lists every object you could track and marks the ones that need Plus.

docs.title: When an org moves from Plus to Free
docs.text:
Nothing is deleted.

  • Intervals, summaries, and archived Intervals stay, and reports and the timeline keep showing them.
  • Objects other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity keep their configuration and their Intervals, but new changes on them are not recorded. The Tracked objects list marks each one "Plus plan: new changes are not recorded", the Health Monitor lists it as information, and Catch up waits until the org is on Plus again, keeping the pause window.
  • The live minute fields stop changing. Breach flags keep updating.
  • A Backfill or purge that is running stops at its next chunk. Purge stops deleting. The Retention screen shows your earlier choice, turned off, with the Plus notice.
  • Omni-Channel agent work is not recorded.

Moving back to Plus resumes all of it with no setup. Changes made while the org was on Free are not replayed.

docs.title: Edition and features
docs.text:
• Salesforce Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, or Developer Edition, in Lightning Experience.
  • Professional Edition is not supported yet: Salesforce runs packaged Apex in Professional Edition only after a package passes its security review.
  • What Sojourn leaves out on purpose, and the limits we know of, are in Scope and limits.
  • Business hours defined in Setup, under Business Hours. Sojourn uses the org default unless you set others.
  • For History backfill (Plus plan): Field History Tracking turned on for the fields you track, before the history you want to keep was written.
  • For Omni-Channel agent work (Plus plan): Omni-Channel turned on, and the Sojourn Omni-Channel package installed after Sojourn.
  • For the timeline on a site: an Experience Cloud site with authenticated members. Guest users cannot see it.

docs.title: People and permissions
docs.text:
• The person who installs needs the System Administrator profile, or the Download AppExchange Packages permission.
  • Admins who set Sojourn up need the Sojourn Admin permission set, and Customize Application to change the overview settings. See Assign permission sets.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Each Interval is a record of about 2 KB in your data storage. When you pick Tracked fields, the object's screen estimates how many rows a month they add and what share of your storage that is a year. On the Plus plan, purge keeps storage in check on large orgs; see Keep or purge Intervals.

You are done when

  • Your org's edition is in the list above.
  • Setup lists at least one active business hours.

docs.title: Keep or purge Intervals
docs.text: Every change to a Tracked field adds an Interval, so a busy org collects millions of rows. Sojourn keeps the totals in summary rows and lets you decide how long the Intervals themselves stay.

docs.title: Summaries come first
docs.text:
Each night the Summaries job counts closed Intervals into daily and monthly summary rows: how many Intervals, how many records, and the total, average, shortest, and longest time, in business and calendar minutes, per object, field, value, owner, and period. Set its time on the Jobs screen, under Operations; see Run the jobs. Report on summaries with the Sojourn Interval Summaries report type; see the Report cookbook.

Summary rows are never purged with Intervals. Daily rows older than the roll-up days, 400 unless you change it, are removed after a complete purge run; monthly rows are kept. See Summaries below.

docs.title: Choose retention
docs.text:
Purge and the archive are on the Plus plan. On the Free plan, every Interval is kept, and the screen shows Keep everything with a note; see Free and Plus plans.

Until you choose, the Sojourn Settings Overview shows Choose how long to keep Intervals, and neither choice is selected on the screen. Open Sojourn Settings, then Data, then Retention and purge:

  • Keep everything: nothing is deleted. Reports read every Interval.
  • Keep N days, from 30 to 3,650: each night after Summaries, closed Intervals older than this are saved to a CSV file and deleted; their summaries are kept.

Choose Save retention; it is off until you pick one. Keeping a number of days asks you to type DELETE first, because a purge deletes records. Days start and end at midnight in the org time zone.

docs.title: Retention per object
docs.text:
Each Tracked object can keep its Intervals for its own number of days, or keep all of them. Set it on the object's Advanced tab, in the Retention card (see The Advanced tab), and save with the object's Save:

  • Use the org's, the default: the object follows the choice on this screen, named beside it, for example "Use the org's: Keep 365 days".
  • Keep this object's Intervals for a number of days, from 30 to 3,650: a purge deletes this object's closed Intervals older than that, and leaves the rest of the org on its own window. The box shows the saved number, or 365 while none is saved; clear it to go back to 365. A number outside 30 to 3,650 is refused, and the notice names the Advanced tab. If such a number reaches the object some other way, through the API or a data load, Sojourn keeps every Interval of that object until its retention is saved again, lists it as "Everything", and writes one Config row to the Error Log saying why.
  • Keep everything for this object: a purge deletes none of this object's Intervals.

An object's own days apply only while the org keeps N days. With the org on Keep everything, nothing is purged, whatever an object is set to: deletion is turned on in one place, here, with DELETE typed. Intervals of an object Sojourn no longer tracks follow the org's window.

The Per object card on this screen lists every Tracked object and what it keeps: "Org's: 365 days" for an object that uses the org's, its own days, such as "90 days", or "Everything". The list is read only; choose an object's name to open its Advanced tab. While the org keeps everything, the card says that a purge deletes nothing until the org keeps N days.

Retention per object is on the Plus plan, with purge. On the Free plan the Retention card shows the object's choice with its controls off and the Plus notice, and the rest of the object still saves. It is not part of a settings file, so moving settings between orgs never changes what an org deletes.

docs.title: What a purge deletes
docs.text:
A purge deletes only Intervals that are closed, already summarised, and ended before their object's cutoff: midnight in the org time zone, that object's number of days ago. Open Intervals are never deleted, however old. A run deletes by one window for each distinct number of days, the org's first, and checks each object's window again at every part, so a change saved during a run applies from its next part.

It works in parts of 2,000 Intervals unless you change the part size (see The purge part size), so a purge of a million Intervals leaves 500 CSV files on its run. Each part is first written to a CSV file, attached to the run's Purge Run record, then deleted in the same step: a part is saved and deleted together, or not at all. The first part that fails stops the run, and the run says why. Choosing Keep everything while a purge runs stops it at its next part, and the run says the rest is kept. Purge now waits while summaries are being built or rebuilt, because a rebuild still reads the Intervals a purge would delete.

Each CSV file has a header row, then one row per Interval, in these columns: Interval, Object, Record Id, Record, Tracked field, From, To, To Id, Entered at, Exited at, Business minutes, Calendar minutes, Owner Id, Owner, Owner type, Source, Goal minutes, Breached, Sequence, Warning, Warned at, Record Closed, Value Group. Times are in UTC; Breached, Warning, and Record Closed are true or false. Record Closed and Value Group are what the summary rows group by: whether the record was closed during the stay, and the value group its value belonged to (blank when the field has no value groups).

The CSV file is your copy. Download it from the Purge Run record before you delete the record or the file. Sojourn never deletes them.

docs.title: The archive
docs.text: Turn on Also copy to the archive to keep each purged Interval in Sojourn's archive object as well. The archive is a big object: the timeline shows its stays (see Show the timeline on a record), and Apex and the API can read it with SOQL, but reports and list views cannot, so a report counts only the Intervals that remain and the summary rows. An archived Interval keeps its values, owner, minutes, goal minutes, and Breach flag, its warning: Warning Flag (1 or 0), Warned At, and Warn Minutes, and what its summary rows group by: Record Closed Flag (1 or 0) and Value Group. Your org includes 1 million archive records; more is a paid add-on from Salesforce. The screen counts the archived Intervals for you: under Purge runs a line reads, for example, "8,090 Intervals archived so far, across 3 purge runs." It adds up what every run listed archived, so it shows from the first run, even when that run archived nothing ("0 Intervals archived so far"), and it does not show while no purge has run. It counts Intervals, not storage, so compare it with the 1 million included. On the Free plan the line is read only. It adds up the runs you can see: if you cannot see every Purge Run record, it counts only the ones you can, and it does not show if you cannot read Purge Run. The CSV file is kept on every run either way.

docs.title: Purge now and the runs
docs.text:
Purge now starts a run straight away, without waiting for the night. The button is on only while the saved choice is Keep N days: on a new install, and under Keep everything, it is off. Its confirmation counts what the run would delete now, for example "4,250 closed, summarised Intervals past their window are saved to a CSV file on the run, then deleted.", and lists each window with its count, such as "The org's 365 days: 4,000 Intervals" and "Lead, 90 days: 250 Intervals", then each object kept whole, such as "Claim: Keep everything, none deleted." Type DELETE to confirm. One purge runs at a time; a second is refused with "A purge is already running. Try again when it finishes."

Purge runs lists each run: when it ran, its status (Queued, Running, Complete, or Failed), how many Intervals it deleted and archived, and how many files it holds; choose the files to open the run. A run counts its Intervals as each part finishes, so a run that stopped part-way shows what it deleted before it stopped. The run's record also keeps Interval Count: how many Intervals the run set out to delete when it started, so you can compare it with what it deleted. Its Message says how many Intervals the run deleted in all and under each window, for example "The org's 365 days: 4,210 deleted. Lead, 90 days: 250 deleted.", and names the objects kept whole. If the org moves to the Free plan while a purge runs, the run deletes nothing from its next part on, keeps the Day summary rows, and its message says so.

docs.title: The purge part size
docs.text: Under the Purge card, open Advanced to set Intervals per purge part, from 50 to 2,000. Each part is saved to one CSV file and deleted in one step, so a smaller part means more, smaller files and less work in each step. The box shows the saved number, or 2,000 while none is saved; clear it to go back to 2,000. Choose Save part size; it saves on its own and asks for no DELETE, because it changes how a purge runs, not what it deletes. A number outside 50 to 2,000 is refused with what to enter. The part size is on the Plus plan, with purge: on the Free plan it shows with its box off and the Plus notice. Reset to defaults on the Advanced screen puts it back to 2,000.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
Open Sojourn Settings, then Summaries under Data.

Roll-up sets Day rows become Month rows after, from 35 to 3,650 days, 400 unless you change it. After a complete purge run, Day rows older than this are removed; their Month rows keep the totals, so reports by month are unchanged, and reports by day reach back this far. The box shows the saved number, or 400 while none is saved; clear it to go back to 400. Choose Save roll-up. A number outside 35 to 3,650 is refused with what to enter. Without purge, as on the Free plan, Day rows are kept.

Rebuild summaries recounts the summary rows of whole months from their Intervals, for example after a backfill. Choose From and To, then Rebuild; the line under the dates names the months it rebuilds. A rebuild is refused for a month a purge has cut into, because its deleted Intervals are no longer there to count, and for a range of more than 9,000 summary rows; rebuild fewer months at a time.

You are done when

  • The Overview no longer asks you to choose retention.
  • With Keep N days, the next morning's Purge Runs list shows a Complete run and its CSV file.

docs.title: Scope and limits
docs.text: Sojourn measures how long records spend in the values of the fields you track, and with each owner. This page lists what it leaves out on purpose, the editions it runs on, how it behaves when your org changes, and the limits we know of.

docs.title: What Sojourn does not do
docs.text:
• It is not an audit trail. Sojourn records only the Tracked fields you choose, and its Intervals can change after they are written: Reconcile and the Health Monitor's repairs close and correct them, and the Sojourn Health Monitor permission set can edit and delete them. Keep Salesforce's own field history for who changed what, on every field.
  • No long text or rich text fields. The field picker offers picklists, lookups, checkboxes, dates, and short text fields; formulas, auto-numbers, and long text are not offered.
  • No setup objects. User, Group, and the other setup objects cannot be tracked; see Track an object.
  • No export to other systems. Sojourn makes no callouts and sends nothing out of your org. Your data leaves only when you take it: by exporting a report, or with the CSV files a purge attaches to its run.

docs.title: How Sojourn records a change
docs.text: Sojourn records each change inside the save that makes it, through its own triggers on Case, Lead, and Opportunity and through a capture Flow on any other object. It uses no Platform Events and no Change Data Capture, so nothing waits in a queue and changes arrive in the order they were saved. Its work counts toward the Salesforce limits of that save, and it leaves a share of each limit for your own automation; see Tune the advanced settings. When Sojourn cannot record a change, the save still succeeds and the Error Log gets a row.

docs.title: Editions
docs.text: Sojourn runs on Salesforce Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, and Developer Edition, in Lightning Experience. Professional Edition is not supported yet. See Check the prerequisites.

docs.title: Encrypted fields
docs.text: Sojourn copies a Tracked field's values onto its Intervals, and no Interval field is encrypted, so a field you encrypt with Shield Platform Encryption is stored in plain text there. For such a field, keep only the change; see Encrypted fields in Track an object.

docs.title: When your org changes
docs.text:
• Records are merged. The Intervals of a record merged away stay with it and are not moved to the record that remains; see When records are merged.
  • An owner is deactivated. Deactivating a user does not change the owner of their records, so their owner stays remain open and keep counting until each record moves to someone else. Reassign the records when the person leaves. The breach alert template emails only active users: a record owned by an inactive user sends no alert, and an inactive manager is left off (see Email a breach alert).
  • A queue is deleted. Before you delete a queue, set it to Use the next rule on the Business hours screen and choose Save, which removes its business hours row. If you delete the queue first, the screen no longer lists it, its row in Queue Business Hours stays unused, and an exported settings file still carries it, so an import in another org skips it with "Queue ... not found in this org." Intervals the queue held keep its name.
  • The org's time zone changes. Sojourn counts days in the org time zone: the Day summary rows, Rebuild summaries, and the purge cutoff. Rows written after the change use the new zone, and rows already written keep their old day boundaries. To count past months again in the new zone, use Rebuild summaries (see Summaries); a month a purge has cut into cannot be rebuilt. The minutes on each Interval do not change.
  • Opportunities use more than one currency. The Opportunity Amount on an Interval is not converted; see Opportunity amounts in more than one currency.

docs.title: People and records Sojourn has to handle
docs.text:
• Integration and API-only users. Sojourn records every save of a Tracked object, whoever makes it, and the person saving needs no Sojourn permission set. Changed By on each Interval names the user. Sojourn has no setting yet to leave out one user's changes; Records to track and Record types on the object's Records tab limit which records are tracked (see The Records tab), and Pause lets a bulk load run without Sojourn's work (see Pause capture during a bulk import).
  • Person Accounts. Not tested yet. A Person Account is an Account record, so tracking one means tracking Account, on the Plus plan, through a capture Flow. Try it in a sandbox first.
  • Experience Cloud guests. The timeline shows to signed-in site users only; guest users cannot see it. See Show the timeline on a record.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Breach and warning flags on open stays change when the Live values job runs. Between runs, an open stay past its goal shows no flag yet, and without Live values scheduled, stays are flagged only when they close. See Run the jobs.
  • Closed by a checkbox. When Closed when reads a checkbox, a record that closes only through that checkbox, with no change to a Tracked field, gets Record Closed at its next tracked change or at the nightly Reconcile, unless the checkbox is itself a Tracked field. See When a record closes.
  • Interval sharing and the timeline. Setting Interval to Private limits reports and list views only. The timeline follows the record's own sharing. See Who sees which Intervals.
  • A retried Case update. Rarely, when Salesforce retries a bulk Case update after refusing one Case in it, a status or owner change your own automation made in that update goes unrecorded until the Case's next change, or until the nightly Reconcile records the value that changed without capture.
  • The archive is not in reports. Archived Intervals show on the timeline and can be read with SOQL from Apex and the API, but reports cannot read them. See The archive.
  • Volume. We have measured Sojourn in scratch orgs, up to 72,003 Intervals, not yet at millions; see Reports at large volume.

You are done when you know which of these apply to your org, and the fields you track hold nothing that some readers of Intervals may not see.

docs.title: Show the timeline on a record
docs.text: The Sojourn timeline shows how long a record spent in each value of its Tracked fields and with each owner: one lane per field, each stay as wide as its share of the time, with totals by value and by owner below.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
• Lanes. One per Tracked field, the status field first and the owner last. Each stay is a segment sized by its business minutes, or calendar minutes when you switch to Calendar. The stay that is still open is Lantern orange and grows until it ends.
  • Colours. A value takes the colour its Tracked field's Value Colours setting gives it: Tide, Harbor, Slate, or Mist. The setting's help text gives its format; Sojourn refuses any other colour on save. Values without one take Tide, Harbor, and Slate in turn, in the order they first appear. Coral and Lantern are kept for Breach and the open stay, so a value never takes them; a queue on the owner lane is always Slate. A field that keeps only the change shows "(hidden)" in the palette's next colour.
  • Goals. A stay with a Goal shows a tick where the goal fell; time past the goal is a red stripe along the bottom of the segment. Turn off Show goal ticks and breach stripes to draw neither.
  • Details. Focus a segment with the keyboard or point at it to see its value, owner, when it began and ended, its business and calendar time, and its goal: how far past it a breached stay went, or that a stay reached its goal's warn percent and is a warning. Press Escape to close it.
  • Totals. Below the lanes, Time by value and Time by owner list each value's time, its share, and its number of stays.
  • History that was purged. When older Intervals were purged to the archive, the timeline also reads the archive and shows those stays dashed, marked as from the archive. Archived stays have no goal marks. Show archived history decides when it looks; see Keep or purge Intervals.
  • Up to date. The card keeps what it last read while the page is open; select Refresh to read the latest Intervals and the minutes so far.
  • Long histories. A record shows its newest 500 Intervals by default, at most 2,000; the timeline says so when older ones are left out. Reports show every Interval.
  • Merged records. After a merge, the record that remains shows only its own stays. The stays of a record merged into it stay with that deleted record and are not moved; see When records are merged.

docs.title: Add it to a record page
docs.text:
1. Open a record of a Tracked object, then Setup (the gear), then Edit Page.
  2. Drag Sojourn Timeline from the Custom components into the page, for example the main column.
  3. Set its properties, then Save and Activate.
Property What it does Fields Tracked fields to show, as API names separated by commas; Owner shows the owner lane. Blank: all. Units Business hours or calendar time when the page opens.
