People can switch on the card. Most Intervals The newest Intervals shown, from 1 to 2,000. The default is 500. Show summary Show Time by value and Time by owner below the lanes. Show goal ticks and breach stripes On by default. Off: no goal ticks, no breach stripes, and no goal in the details or the legend. Show archived history When the archive is on (the default): purged stays show while Sojourn archives or purges. Always: they still show after both are turned off. Never: live Intervals only.

Show archived history never shows more than a person may read: without read on the archive, they see the live Intervals only. Both properties are on record pages and Experience Cloud pages.

docs.title: Who sees it
docs.text: People need the Sojourn Timeline permission, which the Sojourn User, Manager, Health Monitor, and Admin permission sets include; see Assign permission sets. The timeline shows the history of a record only to people who can open that record. Without the permission, the card says so and shows nothing else.

docs.title: Add it to an Experience Cloud page
docs.text:
1. In Experience Builder, open the record page for the object, for example Case Detail.
  2. Drag Sojourn Timeline onto the page and set its properties. To show customers no agent names, set Fields to the status field only, for example Status, and turn off Show summary; tooltips then name no owner either.
  3. Publish the site.
  4. Give site users the Sojourn Site User permission set. It has no user license, so site users can hold it, and it grants only the timeline.

Signed-in site users see the history of records they can open. Guest users are not supported.

Often missed. A site user sees a record's history only if they can open the record itself, through the site's sharing sets or sharing. Sojourn does not share records.

docs.title: When the card is empty
docs.text:
The card says What to do Intervals for this object appear once Sojourn tracks it Track the object in Sojourn Settings; a Sojourn admin sees a link there. The object is tracked through a Flow that is not active Turn the object's capture Flow on; see Track an object. No Intervals yet The first one starts when a Tracked field gets a value or changes. You need the Sojourn Timeline permission Assign a Sojourn permission set that includes it. This record is not shared with you Its history is hidden, as the record is. The timeline shows here on a record page It is placed outside a record page, as in a page builder before a record is chosen; it reads nothing there.

You are done when

  • A record page shows the timeline with a lane for each Tracked field, and focusing a segment shows its details.
  • A person without a Sojourn permission set sees the permission message instead of any history.

docs.title: Track an object
docs.text: You set up tracking in the Sojourn Settings tab of the Sojourn app. The page has a Sojourn menu on the left, in four sections: Capture (Get started, Overview, Tracked objects), Time (Business hours, Goals, Alerts), Data (Retention and purge, Summaries, Export settings), and Operations (Jobs, Health, Advanced). The menu stays in view while a screen scrolls. Choose Collapse menu at its foot to fold it into icons; Sojourn remembers the choice in your browser. The tab needs the Sojourn Admin permission set; without it the page says so and shows nothing else. Changing the org-wide settings, on the Overview and on the Alerts, Jobs, Health, Summaries, Retention and purge, and Advanced screens, also needs the Customize Application permission, which system administrators have.

docs.title: The Overview
docs.text:
The Overview opens first once the Get started guide is done or turned off; until then Sojourn Settings opens on Get started, and the Overview shows a banner that continues it. Three counts lead it: active Tracked objects, paused ones, and open errors, with a link to the Health Monitor. Capture for the whole org holds Tracking enabled and the Default business hours, saved with Save settings. One line says how the jobs stand, with Open Jobs; see Run the jobs.

Usage estimates what Sojourn adds to your data storage, at 2 KB a row, from the Sojourn records you can see:

  • Intervals written this month: the Intervals created since the first of the month, about how many a day, and from how many Tracked objects. A backfilled Interval counts in the month it was written.
  • Storage used by Sojourn: every Interval, summary row, Error Log row, and purge run, at 2 KB a row, and its share of your org's data storage. When the storage limit cannot be read, the tile says so and shows no percent. The archive is a big object, which does not count against data storage.
  • A year at this rate: the storage of a year of Intervals at this month's daily rate. With Keep N days on the Plus plan, it is the Intervals kept at any one time, N days of them and at most a year; with Keep everything, a whole year's.

Usage loads after the rest of the Overview, so a slow count never holds the page up, and a failed one says so on its card only.

docs.title: Add an object
docs.text:
Case, Lead, and Opportunity are tracked on every plan; for the quickest start, see Track Cases and open your first report. Every other object, custom or standard, is on the Plus plan and needs a capture Flow; see Free and Plus plans.

  1. Open the Sojourn app and the Sojourn Settings tab, then Tracked objects in the menu.
  2. Choose Add object, search for the object, pick it, and choose Add object again. The list shows only objects Sojourn can track, so you never type an API name; objects you already track are marked Already tracked.
  3. On the object's screen, open the Fields tab and check the Tracked fields whose time in each value you want; they appear in the table beside the checkboxes, where Remove takes one off and Business hours sets hours for that field alone (leave it on Use the object's to use the object's hours). Picklists, lookups, checkboxes, dates, and short text fields are offered; formulas, auto-numbers, and long text are not. Each field shows its API name under its label, here and in the snapshot fields, and the field lists read "Label (API name)", so two fields with the same label are never confused; search finds a field by either.
  4. Leave Track owner on to measure time with each user and each queue.
  5. Choose Save.

Track only fields that everyone who reads Intervals may see. Sojourn copies a Tracked field's values into each Interval whatever the field-level security of the person who saved the record, and Sojourn User and Sojourn Site User can read those values, so a field you hide from a group shows to that group through Intervals and the timeline.

A Tracked lookup field records the name of the record it points to, not its Id, and Sojourn reads that name whoever saved the change, so the name shows even to people who cannot open that record, for example a record of a private custom object. The owner's name is copied the same way. Track a lookup only when everyone who reads Intervals may see the names of the records it points to.

The same goes for the other record values each Interval carries. Sojourn User can read the record's name (from the Name field below), the owner's name, the record type, and on Case, Lead, and Opportunity the values Sojourn copies there (Case Priority, Origin, and Type; Lead Source and Rating; Opportunity Stage), and the Interval list views show the record and owner names. Intervals are readable by everyone with Sojourn User, whether or not they can open the record, so choose a Name field such as the record number, not one that holds private text such as a Case subject. Snapshot fields and the Opportunity amount are not readable with Sojourn User. The Name field and Snapshot fields lists offer only fields you can read.

An object can have up to 10 Tracked fields, the owner included. From the sixth, the picker reminds you that each field adds Interval rows for every record; at 10, it asks you to turn one off first. Short text fields are listed apart, under "Usually not useful for time in value".

Each Tracked field has Start timing at the first value, on by default. When a record is created with the field blank, timing starts when the field first gets a value, so reports do not count the blank stretch before anyone filled it in. Turn it off to time the blank value from creation as well. The owner always starts at creation. Once a field has had a value, clearing it is a change like any other: the stay in the old value closes and a blank Interval opens, so time spent blank after a value is measured whichever way the switch is set.

Under the picker, the Estimate shows about how many Interval rows a month your choice adds, and how much of your data storage a year that is. It counts the records you can see that were created in the last 30 days and their field history; fields without history are assumed to change once a month. "At least" means the count reached its limit, so the real number is higher.

docs.title: Encrypted fields
docs.text: Sojourn copies a Tracked field's values onto its Intervals, and the Name field and Snapshot fields too, and no Interval field is encrypted. A field you encrypt with Shield Platform Encryption is therefore stored in plain text on its Intervals. For an encrypted Tracked field, choose Only that the value changed under What an Interval keeps on the Values tab (see The Values tab): its Intervals then keep no From or To value, and the time in each stay is still measured. That choice is not offered on the field that decides when a record closes, so keep an encrypted field out of that role, and choose a Name field and Snapshot fields that are not encrypted. In the Tracked fields picker, a field you encrypt carries an Encrypted pill, in the list and once chosen, with a line under it: "Intervals copy its values in plain text. To keep them off, choose Only that the value changed on the Values tab." On the status field, and on the checkbox Closed when reads, the line says only that Intervals copy its values in plain text, because that choice is not offered there. The picker marks only Tracked fields; check the Name field and Snapshot fields in Setup.

docs.title: The object's tabs
docs.text:
An object's screen keeps its header at the top: the object, its capture pill, Active, and Pause. Below it, six tabs hold its settings. Choose a tab, or move along the tab row with the arrow keys, Home, and End.

  • Fields: the Tracked fields, Track owner, and the Estimate.
  • Values: for each Tracked field, the values that do not count, value groups, colours on the timeline, and what an Interval keeps; and which owners get an Interval (see The Values tab).
  • Records:
    • Status field and Closed values: the main status field and the values that mean the record is closed (see When a record closes).
    • Name field: the field shown as the record's name on each Interval.
    • Record types: track only these record types; leave empty for all.
    • Business hours, or Business hours from a record field: the hours used for this object's business minutes.
    • Snapshot fields: up to 5 fields copied onto each Interval, for grouping reports by values such as priority.
    • Records to track: conditions a record must meet to get Intervals; leave empty to track every record (see The Records tab).
    • Business hours by record type: the business hours for each record type of the object (see The Records tab).
  • Backfill: give existing records their Intervals, with the last backfill and the last Catch up; see Backfill past Intervals.
  • Live values: Write live values to the record and its two minute fields, number fields on the record for the minutes in the current status and with the current owner. The Live values job keeps them current on the schedule set on the Jobs screen (see Live values and the jobs).
  • Advanced: the Retention card, how long this object's Intervals are kept, and the Capture card, with the lookup Sojourn fills on each Interval and the History backfill's records per chunk (see The Advanced tab).

Save, at the foot of every tab, saves the changes on every tab together: change the fields on one tab and the settings on another, then save once. Switching tabs keeps what you changed. If a value cannot be saved, nothing is saved, and the notice names the tab that holds it, for example "Check the Records tab. Choose at most 5 snapshot fields." The address names the open tab, so you can copy a link to it; see Links into Sojourn.

docs.title: The Values tab
docs.text:
Choose a field in Tracked field, with the status field first; each field keeps its own settings, and they are saved with Save like every other tab. A picklist offers its values, a checkbox offers Checked and Not checked, and for a text field you type a value and press Enter.

  • Do not count these values: a change into one of these values closes the open Interval at the change and opens none, so the clock stops; the next change to a counted value opens an Interval whose From is the value the record left when the change carries it (a save, a Flow that passes the prior record, or repair) or when the field has only one value that does not count; otherwise, as after a Catch up, Reconcile, or Seed backfill, From is blank. Use it for a value such as Waiting on Customer. Blank always counts, and on the status field a closed value always counts, so neither is offered. A goal on a value that does not count never applies, and the Goals screen leaves those values out.
  • Value groups: name a group, up to 80 characters, and add its values; a value can be in one group. Add a group adds a row and Remove takes one away. Each new Interval carries its value's group in Value Group, so reports and summaries can count Backlog as one. A change to the groups applies to Intervals opened after it.
  • Colours on the timeline: Tide, Harbor, Slate, or Mist for each value, or Automatic for the timeline's own order. Coral stays for a Breach and Lantern for the current Interval, so neither is offered. The timeline draws each value's stays in its colour (see Show the timeline on a record).
  • What an Interval keeps: Each value, from and to, the default, or Only that the value changed, for a field whose values are private. With only the change, new Intervals of the field keep From, To, and the group blank, the timeline shows "(hidden)", and an Error Log row for a change it could not record keeps no From or To value either; minutes, the owner, and the sequence are kept, and repair still places such a change by its time. It is not offered on the field that decides when a record is closed, the status field or the checkbox Closed when reads, because the close figures and Record Closed read their values, nor on a field with active goals, which need the values; the tab says which. Intervals already written keep what they hold. A field that keeps only the change is recorded by a save and by a Flow that passes the prior record; Catch up, Reconcile, Seed backfill, and a Flow without the prior record cannot tell that its value changed, so they leave its open Interval as it is.

The Owner card shows while the object tracks its owner. Track sets which owners get an Interval: Users and queues, the default, Users only, or Queues only. Ignore a move between members of the same queue keeps one owner stay when the record moves from one direct member of a queue that takes this object to another; leave it off when reports count time per person.

  • Users only: no owner Interval opens while a queue owns the record. A move to a queue closes the user's stay at the move, and the next user's stay continues the sequence, with From set to the queue the record left. When a Case or Lead assignment rule sends a new record to a queue in the save that creates it, the creator's stay closes at its own start, a stay of 0 minutes; nothing is deleted.
  • Queues only: the reverse. No owner Interval opens while a user owns the record, and a move to a user closes the queue's stay.
  • Ignore a move between members of the same queue: the stay keeps the owner it started with while the record moves between users who are both direct members of one queue that takes this object; a move to anyone else closes it. Users who belong through a role or a nested public group are not direct members. Sojourn reads the queue's members once per save, and which objects each queue takes in system mode, so a user without View Setup and Configuration gets the same result.

Capture, Flow capture, Catch up, Reconcile, and History backfill all follow these choices. A change applies from the next owner change on each record; Intervals already written stay as they are.

If a value cannot be saved, nothing is saved and the notice says so, for example "Check the Values tab. Escalated is a closed value, so it always counts."

docs.title: The Records tab
docs.text:
Below Object settings, two more cards:

  • Records to track: only records that match every condition get Intervals. Add a condition adds a row; choose the Field, equal to or not equal to, and the Value, and Remove takes a row away. The fields are the object's picklist, checkbox, and short text fields you can read. A picklist offers its values, a checkbox offers Checked and Not checked with equal to only, and for a text field you type the value; an empty box matches a blank field. Leave the card empty to track every record. Sojourn checks the conditions on the record's values after each save, as it checks Record types: a record that stops matching keeps its open Intervals, and new changes are not recorded until it matches again; then its next change is recorded, and Reconcile repairs what changed meanwhile. A History backfill applies the conditions too.
  • Business hours by record type: one row for each record type of the object, set to business hours or left on Use the next rule. A record of that type uses those hours ahead of the queue's and the object's; the Tracked field's own hours and the record's business hours field still win (see Business hours for each Interval). An object with no record types shows no rows: its records use the Business hours under Object settings.

If a condition or a record type's hours cannot be saved, nothing is saved and the notice names the tab, for example "Check the Records tab. Description on Case cannot be a condition. Choose a picklist, checkbox, or short text field."

docs.title: The Advanced tab
docs.text:
• Retention: how long a purge keeps this object's closed Intervals. Use the org's, the default, follows Retention and purge and names its window, for example "Use the org's: Keep 365 days". Keep this object's Intervals for a number of days, from 30 to 3,650, gives the object its own window; typing in the box chooses it, and the box shows 365 while no number is saved. Keep everything for this object keeps all of them. The object's own days apply only while the org keeps N days: with the org on Keep everything, nothing is deleted. It is on the Plus plan, with purge: on the Free plan it shows with its controls off and the Plus notice, and the rest of the object still saves. See Retention per object.
  • Lookup to fill on each Interval shows only when two or more lookups on Interval point to this object, for example a lookup to Case that you added to Interval beside Sojourn's own. Sojourn fills one of them with the record on every new Interval. Automatic, the default, fills the lookup named after the object, or else the first; choose another to fill that one instead. Only lookups on Interval that point to this object are offered.
  • History backfill: records per chunk: how many records a History backfill reads at a time, from 5 to 50, 20 unless you change it. Each chunk reads every field change of its records, so choose fewer when records have long field history. The box shows the saved number, or 20 while none is saved; clear it to go back to 20. It is on the Plus plan, with History backfill: on the Free plan it shows with its box off and the Plus notice, and the rest of the object still saves. See Backfill past Intervals.

docs.title: When a record closes
docs.text:
A record counts as closed while its status field holds one of the Closed values. When the Tracked object's Closed Checkbox Field names a checkbox on the object, such as IsClosed on Opportunity, the record counts as closed while that checkbox is checked instead, and the closed values no longer decide. The list offers every checkbox on the object except Deleted (IsDeleted), which a live record never has checked. A name that is not a checkbox on the object, or IsDeleted, is ignored, with a Config row in the Error Log, and the closed values decide.

While a record is closed:

  • every Interval open on it carries Record Closed, and so does every Interval that opens while it stays closed. An Interval that ends while the record is closed keeps the flag, and so does the one the reopen ends, such as the closed status;
  • the owner's stay ends at the close, with its minutes as usual, and no Owner Interval opens, even when the owner changes;
  • when the record reopens, a new Owner Interval opens for the owner it has then. Intervals still open after the reopen lose Record Closed, because the record is live again, and Intervals that open from then on do not carry it.

History and Seed backfill, Catch up, and the nightly Reconcile follow the same rule; History reads the deciding field's history, and without it a closed record counts as closed since its last change (see Backfill). Reconcile also puts Record Closed in step on the open Intervals of the records it checks and ends their open owner stays, at the entry of the Interval that holds the closed value when there is one, otherwise at the record's last modification.

docs.title: Check that capture is live
docs.text:
Each Tracked object shows a pill:

Pill Meaning Tracked by package Case, Lead, and Opportunity: Sojourn's own triggers capture every change. Flow active An active Sojourn capture Flow runs on this object. Flow missing No capture Flow runs yet. Follow the steps on the object's screen. Flow unknown Sojourn could not read your Flows, usually because you lack View Setup and Configuration. Paused Capture is paused for a bulk import. Inactive The object is configured but not tracked.

While an object's pill reads Flow missing or Flow unknown, its screen leads with four steps, and its fields and settings show as summaries until you choose Edit fields or Edit settings. On the Tracked objects list, Set up Flow opens those steps and Re-check Flows checks every object at once:

  1. In Setup, open Flows and the Sojourn Capture Template, then choose Save As, a new Flow. Keep "Sojourn" in the label.
  2. On the Start element, choose your object.
  3. In Sojourn: Capture Change, set the object for Record and Prior record to the same object. Pass the prior record on every save, as the template does: when some saves in one batch pass it and others do not, Sojourn records each correctly but in two passes, at twice the queries. (Sprint 13: Flow Builder shows the action's two inputs in one section, Record change, with Record first and Prior record under it, in place of its alphabetical list.)
  4. Activate the Flow, then choose Re-check on the object's screen. The pill turns to Flow active.

Keep your copy a record-triggered Flow that runs after the save, as the template is: it runs in system context, so it records every user's changes. If you call Sojourn: Capture Change from a screen Flow or another Flow that runs as the user, give those users access to the action's Apex class (ChangeCapture) through a permission set of your own; only Sojourn Admin includes it, and without it the Flow fails for everyone else. Grant it with care: the action records the field values and change time of the record the Flow hands it, without reading the record again, so a Flow that changes that record variable before the action, run by a user with the class, records Intervals for values the record never held.

If both a trigger and a Flow capture the same change in one save, Sojourn records it once. Each Interval records how the change arrived in its Source field: Trigger, Flow, or Catch-Up.

Often missed. Setup objects such as User and Group cannot be tracked. Salesforce does not allow their changes and Sojourn's Intervals to be saved in one transaction, so Sojourn leaves them out of the list.

docs.title: Pause capture during a bulk import
docs.text:
The Tracked objects list shows each object's Tracked fields, whether it tracks the owner, its capture pill, and where its business hours come from: named hours, From record field, or Sojourn default.

Choose Pause on the Tracked object, in the list or on its screen, before a large import or update, and Resume afterwards. The list shows when the pause started. To stop tracking an object, turn off Active on its screen and choose Save; Turn on in the list brings it back. A notice at the top of the page says each took effect, for example "Case is paused. Changes made now wait for Catch up." While paused, triggers and Flows skip the object, so the import runs without Sojourn's work. After you resume, the list says "Changes made while paused wait for Catch up". Choose Catch up to replay the records changed during the pause: each gets its Interval at the time it changed (its last modification, or its creation if it was created during the pause), and values Sojourn already holds are skipped, so running it twice is safe. A field with no open Interval gets its first one only on a record created during the pause; on older records it waits for the field's next change, and a blank field timed from its first value gets nothing until it has one. One catch up runs at a time across all objects: while one is going, the list says "Catch up is running" in place of the button, and starting another is refused. If part of the run is skipped or fails (for example, tracking was turned off, or the Error Log records a Limit or DML error), the list keeps offering Catch up, so you can run it again. If you pause the object while a catch up runs, even briefly and resumed before it ends, the pause window is kept for the next catch up. Pausing again before you catch up keeps the earlier start, so one catch up covers both pauses. The result of the last catch up is kept in the Tracked object record's Catch Up Message field, apart from the last backfill result, so a catch up never hides how the backfill went; the object's screen lists both in its Backfill card, as Last backfill and Last Catch up.

Importing past records. When an import sets each record's Created Date (Salesforce's Set Audit Fields upon Record Creation), Cases, Leads, and Opportunities start their first Intervals at that date. A Flow cannot tell a new record from an update, so for other objects also set Last Modified Date to the Created Date in the import; otherwise their first Intervals start at the import.

docs.title: Backfill past Intervals
docs.text: A new object starts with the next change. To give existing records their Intervals, use the Backfill tab of the object's screen; see Backfill past Intervals.

docs.title: Live values and the jobs
docs.text: The Jobs screen, under Operations, schedules Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries, and runs each now. See Run the jobs for when each runs and what it does.

docs.title: Business hours for each Interval
docs.text:
Sojourn uses the first of these that is set:

  1. The Tracked field's business hours.
  2. A business hours field on the record, chosen in Business hours from a record field.
  3. The record type's business hours, set in Business hours by record type on the Records tab.
  4. The queue's entry in Queue Business Hours, while a queue owns the record.
  5. The Tracked object's business hours.
  6. The default on the Sojourn Settings overview.
  7. The org default business hours.

If none applies, or the chosen business hours no longer exist, the Interval gets calendar minutes as business minutes, and an Error Log row of type BusinessHours tells you which setting to fix. A save, or an Omni-Channel agent work change, writes the row for the business hours it could not use. Live values, Reconcile, and backfill write it too, once while a row with the same words is open, so a job that meets the same business hours on every run adds no second row until you resolve the first. The record timeline and Sojourn Dashboards count calendar minutes the same way and write no row.

docs.title: When records are merged
docs.text: When you merge records, for example two Leads or two Cases, Salesforce keeps one record and deletes the others. The Intervals of a deleted record stay with it: they keep its record Id in Parent Id, and Sojourn does not move them onto the record that remains. The nightly Reconcile closes each Interval still open on the deleted record at the time it was deleted, and checks Orphaned on all of its Intervals (see Run the jobs). Salesforce itself moves the Interval's lookup to the record (for example Lead or Case) onto the record that remains, so report types that start from that record list the merged stays under it. The timeline reads Parent Id, so the remaining record's timeline shows only its own stays, and time with each owner before the merge stays on the record where it was spent. For reports, see Merged and deleted records in the cookbook.

docs.title: The Error Log
docs.text:
Sojourn never fails your users' saves. If it cannot record a change, it writes an Error Log row instead; the overview shows how many are open and opens the Health Monitor, which explains each error and fixes it. See Watch Sojourn in the Health Monitor. To stop all capture at once, turn off Tracking enabled on the overview and choose Save settings.

You are done when the object's pill reads Tracked by package or Flow active, and changing a Tracked field on a record opens a new Interval for it and closes the previous one.

docs.title: Track Cases and open your first report
docs.text: Case, Lead, and Opportunity are tracked by the package's own triggers, on every plan, so they need no Flow.

docs.title: Track Cases
docs.text:
1. Open the Sojourn app, the Sojourn Settings tab, then Tracked objects in the menu.
  2. Choose Add object, search for Case, pick it, and choose Add object again.
  3. On the Case screen, check Status, and any other field whose time in each value you want, such as Priority.
  4. Leave Track owner on to measure time with each user and each queue.
  5. On the Records tab, under Closed when, keep Status and leave Closed values empty: Sojourn then counts every case status marked Closed in Setup as closed. List values only to replace that list, and list every status that closes a case, since a status left out stops counting as closed.
  6. Choose Save.

docs.title: Cases and Leads routed by assignment rules
docs.text:
When an assignment rule routes a new Case or Lead, for example from Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, Web-to-Lead, or an import that uses the default rule, Sojourn records the owner the rule chose as the record's first owner, from the moment the record was created. Salesforce runs assignment rules after the save that creates the record, in the same transaction, and Sojourn treats an owner set there as part of creating the record:

  • the first Owner Interval names the queue or user the rule chose, not the user who created the record (for Email-to-Case, the Automated Case User);
  • the first Status Interval names that owner too;
  • the Case's Owner Change Count does not count the routing.

An owner change in any later save, by a person, a Flow, or a rule run on edit, closes the Owner Interval and opens the next one as usual. While the Case is closed no Owner Interval is open: closing the Case ends the owner's stay, and reopening it starts a new one (see When a record closes).

docs.title: Turn on the jobs
docs.text: The Jobs screen, under Operations, schedules the three jobs that keep Intervals current; Open Jobs on the Overview opens it. Choose Turn on for Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries. See Run the jobs for what each does.

docs.title: Open your first report
docs.text:
1. Change the status of a Case.
  2. Open the Reports tab and the Sojourn Reports folder.
  3. Open Time in Status by Case. The Case appears with its time in each status, in business hours.

You are done when

  • The Case's Intervals tab lists one Interval for each status it has had.
  • Time in Status by Case shows the Case with the time in its earlier status.

Other objects, custom or standard, are tracked through a capture Flow on the Plus plan; see Track an object.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the Health Monitor: it checks capture, the jobs, and the Error Log, and says how to fix each problem it finds.

docs.title: A change made no Interval
docs.text: Check Fix Tracking enabled is off on the Sojourn Settings overview Turn it on. Reconcile records the values that changed meanwhile The object is paused or inactive Resume or Turn on it on the Tracked objects list, then Catch up The field is not a Tracked field Check it on the object's screen and choose Save; capture starts with the next change The object's pill reads Flow missing or Flow unknown Activate its capture Flow, as the object's screen shows; see Track an object The Health Monitor shows "Plus plan needed" for the object Objects other than Case, Lead, and Opportunity need the Plus plan; see Free and Plus plans The record type is not in Record types Add it, or leave the list empty to track every record type The Error Log has a Limit or DML row for the change Create interval on the error recreates it; Reconcile also retries it each night

docs.title: A report is empty or out of date
docs.text:
• Reports on Interval Summaries read the summary rows, which the Summaries job writes each night. Turn it on, or choose Rebuild on the Summaries screen for past months.
  • Reports read only the Intervals and records you can see. Check the report runs as a user with the Sojourn Manager or Sojourn User permission set.
  • A report that runs past 10 minutes stops; filter it to fewer records or days. See Reports at large volume.

docs.title: The timeline is empty
docs.text: The timeline says why in its empty state: the object is not tracked, its Flow is not active, the record has no Intervals yet, you lack the Sojourn Timeline permission, or the record is not shared with you. See Show the timeline on a record.

docs.title: A backfill failed
docs.text:
History backfill needs Field History Tracking on the fields. The Health Monitor names the error; choose Seed or Fresh instead, or turn on history and run it again. History and Seed are on the Plus plan.

A run that stopped part-way shows Failed with the records it finished and what stopped it, for example a Salesforce limit in one job of the chain; run it again, and the records already done are skipped. See How a run works.

docs.title: Hear about errors without opening the Health Monitor
docs.text: Subscribe to a copy of the Error Log by Type report, so an email arrives on the mornings an error needs you; see Email me when Sojourn logs an error in the cookbook.

docs.title: What to send us
docs.text:
When you ask us for help, send what you can of this list. It lets us answer without asking twice.

  • The versions. In Setup, Installed Packages: the version number of Sojourn, and of Sojourn Omni-Channel if you have it.
  • The org. Its edition, whether it is production or a sandbox, and whether Sojourn Settings shows the Plus notices, which means it is on the Free plan.
  • The Health Monitor. A screenshot of its Overview: the banner, Capture, Jobs, and Errors.
  • The errors. For each Error Log row involved: its Error Number, Error Type, the object, when it happened, and the message. Open the row on the Health Monitor's Errors tab to see them. The technical details, which only a Sojourn admin sees, help most; read them first, because a message can hold a record's values.
  • The settings. The file from Export settings (see Move settings between orgs). It holds your configuration, not your records.
  • What happened. The record Id, the change you made and when, and what you expected to see.

Never send a password or a link that signs in to your org.

docs.title: Uninstall Sojourn
docs.text: Uninstalling deletes every Sojourn object and its records: Intervals, summaries, Tracked objects, goals, the Error Log, and the archive. It also deletes the permission sets, reports, and dashboards that came with the package. Records outside Sojourn, such as your Cases, are not changed. The CSV files that purge saved are Salesforce Files owned by the admin who ran purge; they stay after the uninstall.

docs.title: Before you uninstall
docs.text:
1. In Sojourn Settings, open Jobs under Operations and Turn off each job: Live values, Reconcile, and Summaries.
  2. Wait for any Backfill, Catch up, or purge that is running to finish; the Health Monitor shows them.
  3. To keep the configuration, export it from Export settings; see Move settings between orgs.
  4. Remove the Sojourn permission sets from every user: in Setup, open Permission Sets, then each Sojourn set, then Manage Assignments. Salesforce refuses the uninstall while one is assigned.
  5. Remove anything you built on Sojourn's objects outside the package, such as your own reports, Flows, or fields on the Interval object. Salesforce refuses an uninstall while another component refers to a package component.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. If Sojourn Omni-Channel is installed, uninstall it first.
  2. In Setup, open Installed Packages, choose Uninstall next to Sojourn, and confirm.
  3. To keep the data, choose to save a copy of the package's data before it is deleted. Salesforce emails a link when the uninstall finishes; the export files are deleted two days after that.

You are done when

  • Installed Packages no longer lists Sojourn.
  • Scheduled Jobs in Setup lists no Sojourn job.

docs.title: Case
docs.text:
API name: Case

Field API name Type Description Sojourn Agent Business Minutes Agent_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes the Case spent owned by users, summed over its closed Owner Intervals; the open owner stay adds once it closes. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case (a save, a Backfill, a repair) and writes it only when it changes. Needs the owner tracked on Case (Track Owner). Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: Total business minutes users have owned this Case, from its finished owner stays. Sojourn sets it; an edit is replaced the next time it recomputes. Sojourn First Close Business Minutes First_Close_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes from the Case's creation to its first close: the sum of the closed Intervals, before the first closed value, of the field Closed when reads (the status field, or the closed checkbox). Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case and writes it only when it changes. Blank until the Case first closes; a reopen does not change it.Help text: Business minutes from creation to the first close, across all statuses. Sojourn sets it; blank until the Case first closes. Sojourn First Closed At First_Closed_At__c DateTime When the Case first closed: the Entered At of its first Interval in a closed value, by the Tracked object's Closed when setting (a closed status value, or the closed checkbox). Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case. Blank until the Case first closes; reopening does not change it.Help text: Set by Sojourn the first time the case closes. Reopening does not change it. Sojourn Owner Business Minutes Owner_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes the Case has spent with its current owner: the business minutes to date of its open Owner Interval. Written by each Live values run on the Plus plan, when Live values is on for the Case Tracked object and the owner is tracked; an owner stay older than the Live values window is not refreshed, and a closed Case keeps its last value. Blank until the first such run. For list views, reports, and your own automation.Help text: How long, in business minutes, the Case has been with its current owner. Sojourn refreshes it on each Live values run, on the Plus plan with Live values on; blank until then. Sojourn Owner Change Count Owner_Change_Count__c Number (9, 0) Handoffs: how many of the Case's Owner Intervals have a different owner from the one before. A reopen that goes back to the same owner is not a handoff. A whole number, 0 for a Case never reassigned. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case; needs the owner tracked (Track Owner). Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: Handoffs between owners. A case that was never reassigned shows 0. Sojourn Queue Business Minutes Queue_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes the Case spent owned by queues, summed over its closed Owner Intervals; the open owner stay adds once it closes. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case (a save, a Backfill, a repair) and writes it only when it changes. Needs the owner tracked on Case (Track Owner). Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: Total business minutes queues have owned this Case, from its finished owner stays: time waiting to be picked up. Sojourn sets it. Sojourn Reopen Count Reopen_Count__c Number (9, 0) Times the Case went from a closed value back to an open one, by the Tracked object's Closed when setting (a closed status value, or the closed checkbox). A whole number, 0 when never reopened. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case; the Reopened Cases by Agent report reads it. Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: Times the Case was reopened after closing. Sojourn sets it. Sojourn State Business Minutes State_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes the Case has spent in its current status (the Tracked object's Status Field): the business minutes to date of its open status Interval. Written by each Live values run on the Plus plan, when Live values is on for the Case Tracked object; a stay older than the Live values window is not refreshed, and a closed Case keeps its last value. Blank until the first such run. For list views, reports, and your own automation.Help text: How long, in business minutes, the Case has been in its current status. Sojourn refreshes it on each Live values run, on the Plus plan with Live values on; blank until then. Sojourn Status Change Count Status_Change_Count__c Number (9, 0) Status changes after creation: the number of the Case's status field Intervals minus one, since the first holds the value the Case started with. A whole number, 0 when the status never changed. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case. Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: How many times the Case's status changed after it was created. Sojourn sets it. Sojourn Total Business Minutes Total_Business_Minutes__c Number (16, 2) Business minutes across the Case's closed Owner Intervals: Queue Business Minutes plus Agent Business Minutes. The open owner stay adds once it closes. Sojourn recomputes it from the Case's Intervals whenever it writes Intervals for the Case; needs the owner tracked (Track Owner). Blank until Sojourn first computes it.Help text: Total business minutes of this Case's finished owner stays, with queues and with users. Sojourn sets it.

Field API name Type Description Filters Filters__c LongTextArea (4000) The filters every chart on the dashboard follows, as JSON: {"objectApi": a Tracked object, "field": a Tracked field's API name, "period": 7, 30, or 90 days, "hours": "business" or "calendar", "ownerId": a user Id, left out for all owners}.
